nodes.body:
# MCP Protocol Layer

The MCP (Model Context Protocol) layer is the external-facing boundary of the
`openproject-mcp-server` application. It exposes OpenProject data and operations
to MCP clients (e.g. AI assistants) through a Spring AI MCP server running over
HTTP with the SSE transport.

## Configuration and Transport

The server is configured in
[application.properties](../../src/main/resources/application.properties):

```properties
spring.ai.mcp.server.enabled=true
spring.ai.mcp.server.name=openproject-mcp-server
spring.ai.mcp.server.version=1.2.0
spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol=sse
spring.ai.mcp.server.capabilities.tool=true
spring.ai.mcp.server.type=sync
spring.ai.mcp.server.annotation-scanner.enabled=true
```

Key configuration points:

- **Protocol**: `sse` is the production transport. The server listens on `/mcp`
  (JSON-RPC endpoint) and `/sse` (SSE server-sent events endpoint). Tests
  override this to `STREAMABLE` to avoid keeping open HTTP streams during test
  execution
  [McpToolsListIntegrationTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsListIntegrationTest.java].
- **Sync type**: `sync` means tool invocations are handled synchronously within
  the HTTP request lifecycle, not on background threads.
- **Annotation scanner**: Enabled so that `@McpTool` and `@McpPrompt`
  annotations on Spring `@Component` beans are auto-discovered at startup.

## Tool Registration

All tool beans are `@Component` classes in the
`de.tklein.tklab.openproject.mcp.tools` package. Spring AI's annotation scanner
discovers them at startup and registers each `@McpTool`-annotated method as an
MCP tool with the server.

### Tool Classes

There are six tool classes:

1. **PriorityTools** — provides `priorityList()` to retrieve available priority
   values from OpenProject
   [PriorityTools][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/PriorityTools.java].
2. **ProjectTools** — provides `projectList()` and the prompt
   `openproject.project.summary`
   [ProjectTools][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/ProjectTools.java].
3. **RelationTools** — provides six tools for work package relations:
   `relationAllowedValues()`, `relationList()`, `relationAdd()`,
   `relationDelete()`, `relationAddParent()`, `relationDeleteParent()`
   [RelationTools][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/RelationTools.java].
   The `RelationType` enum defines six relation kinds: `relates`, `blocks`,
   `precedes`, `duplicates`, `includes`, `requires`.
4. **TypesTools** — provides `typeList(projectId)` to list allowed work package
   types for a given project
   [TypesTools][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/TypesTools.java].
5. **WorkPackageTools** — the most feature-rich tool class with seven tools:
   `workPackageList()`, `workPackageShow()`, `workPackageCreate()`,
   `workPackageUpdate()`, `workPackageUploadAttachment()`, plus the prompt
   `openproject.workpackage.safe_edit`
   [WorkPackageTools][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/WorkPackageTools.java].
6. **Common** — provides `handleLoggingMessage()` for MCP client log
   notifications, tagged with `@McpLogging(clients = "openproject-mcp-server")`
   [Common][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/Common.java].

### Tool Annotations

Each tool method carries `@McpTool(description = "...")` which defines the tool
name (derived from the method name) and its human-readable description. The
`annotations = @McpAnnotations(readOnlyHint = true)` flag marks read-only tools
so MCP clients can optimize their behavior.

Validation is handled via `@Validated` on the class level and
`@NotNull`/`@JsonProperty` annotations on parameters. Spring AI converts these
into the tool's `inputSchema` (JSON Schema) that appears in `tools/list`
responses.

### JSON-RPC `tools/list` Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server
    participant Scanner
    participant Tools

    Client->>Server: POST /mcp (initialize)
    Server-->>Client: SSE session established
    Client->>Server: JSON-RPC tools/list
    Server->>Scanner: Discover @McpTool beans
    Scanner-->>Server: list of tool descriptors
    Server->>Tools: build inputSchema from annotations
    Server-->>Client: tools/list result (14 tools)
```

The `tools/list` response contains all 14 tool descriptors, each with `name`,
`description`, and `inputSchema`
[McpToolsListIntegrationTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsListIntegrationTest.java].

### JSON-RPC `prompts/list` Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server
    participant Scanner
    participant Prompts

    Client->>Server: POST /mcp (initialize)
    Server-->>Client: SSE session established
    Client->>Server: JSON-RPC prompts/list
    Server->>Scanner: Discover @McpPrompt beans
    Scanner-->>Server: list of prompt descriptors
    Server-->>Client: prompts/list result (2 prompts)
```

Two prompts are registered:

- **`openproject.project.summary`** — takes `projectId` and `projectName`
  arguments, returns a `GetPromptResult` with an assistant message template
  [ProjectTools][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/ProjectTools.java].
- **`openproject.workpackage.safe_edit`** — takes `workPackageId` and
  `requestedChange` arguments, returns a detailed system prompt that instructs
  the AI assistant to follow a diff-then-confirm workflow for safe work package
  updates, including lockVersion concurrency handling and Markdown newline
  conventions
  [WorkPackageTools][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/WorkPackageTools.java].

## JSON-RPC Initialization

The MCP protocol requires a client to call `initialize` before using any other
method. The flow is:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server
    participant AuthFilter

    Client->>Server: POST /mcp with initialize request
    AuthFilter->>AuthFilter: validate Bearer token
    AuthFilter-->>Server: auth success
    Server-->>Client: SSE response with session ID
    Note over Client,Server: Subsequent requests use Mcp-Session-Id header
```

The client sends a JSON-RPC 2.0 `initialize` request to `/mcp` with:
- `protocolVersion`: `"2024-11-05"`
- `capabilities`: client capabilities object
- `clientInfo`: `{ name, version }`

The server responds over the SSE stream with:
- A `Mcp-Session-Id` HTTP header (required for all subsequent requests)
- A JSON-RPC response containing the server's protocol version, capabilities,
  and server info

After initialization, all subsequent JSON-RPC calls must include the
`Mcp-Session-Id` header
[McpToolsHelper][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsHelper.java].

## JSON-RPC `tools/call` Flow

When a client calls a tool:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant AuthFilter
    participant Server
    participant ToolBean
    participant ApiClient
    participant OpenProject

    Client->>AuthFilter: POST /mcp + Mcp-Session-Id + Bearer token
    AuthFilter->>AuthFilter: validate token against OpenProject
    AuthFilter->>AuthFilter: cache validation (Caffeine, 60 min)
    AuthFilter-->>Server: auth success
    Server->>ToolBean: invoke @McpTool method
    ToolBean->>ApiClient: call OpenProject REST API
    ApiClient->>OpenProject: HTTP request (HAL+JSON)
    OpenProject-->>ApiClient: response JSON
    ApiClient-->>ToolBean: mapped DTOs
    ToolBean-->>Server: result
    Server-->>Client: JSON-RPC response
```

Each tool method delegates to `OpenProjectApiClient`, which uses `RestClient`
with HAL+JSON content negotiation to call the OpenProject REST API v3
[OpenProjectApiClient][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java].
The `OpenProjectRestClientFactory` builds the `RestClient` per request by
resolving the connection details (base URL and authorization header) from the
current HTTP request
[OpenProjectRestClientFactory][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestClientFactory.java].

## JSON-RPC `prompts/get` Flow

When a client retrieves a prompt:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server
    participant PromptBean

    Client->>Server: JSON-RPC prompts/get with name + arguments
    Server->>PromptBean: invoke @McpPrompt method
    PromptBean->>PromptBean: build GetPromptResult with template
    PromptBean-->>Server: GetPromptResult
    Server-->>Client: JSON-RPC response with messages
```

The prompt methods are regular Spring beans — they receive arguments from the
client, apply them to a string template, and return a `GetPromptResult`
containing a list of `PromptMessage`s. The `safe_edit` prompt returns a
comprehensive system prompt that enforces a diff-then-confirm workflow with
lockVersion-based concurrency control
[WorkPackageTools][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/WorkPackageTools.java].

## JSON-RPC `ping`

The `ping` method is a standard MCP health check. The server responds with an
empty result object
[McpPingIntegrationTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpPingIntegrationTest.java].

## Authentication and Security

The MCP layer sits behind two Spring Security filter chains:

1. **Actuator chain** (`/actuator/**`) — basic auth with admin role for health
   endpoints
   [SecurityConfig][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java].
2. **MCP chain** (`/mcp/**`, `/sse`) — Bearer token authentication via
   `McpBearerAuthenticationFilter`

### Bearer Token Flow

`McpBearerAuthenticationFilter` extends `OncePerRequestFilter` and intercepts
all `/mcp` and `/sse` requests:

1. Extracts the Bearer token from the `Authorization` header
   [McpBearerAuthenticationFilter][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java].
2. Delegates to `OpenProjectTokenValidator` which:
   - Resolves the OpenProject base URL via `OpenProjectConnectionResolver`
   - Hashes `baseUrl|token` with SHA-256 as a cache key
   - Checks `OpenProjectTokenValidationCache` (Caffeine, 60 min TTL)
   - On cache miss, calls `OpenProjectApiClient.root()` to validate the token
     against OpenProject's `/api/v3` endpoint
   - Caches the result keyed by the token hash
   [OpenProjectTokenValidator][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java].
3. Sets a `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` with role `ROLE_MCP_USER` in
   `SecurityContextHolder` and saves the context via
   `RequestAttributeSecurityContextRepository` for async dispatch restoration.
4. On validation failure, returns HTTP 401 with `{"error":"unauthorized"}`
   [McpBearerAuthenticationFilter][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java].

The `McpBearerAuthenticationFilter` is explicitly **not** registered as a global
servlet filter (disabled via `FilterRegistrationBean`), so it only runs inside
the MCP security filter chain
[SecurityConfig][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java].

### Connection Resolution

Two implementations of `OpenProjectConnectionResolver` exist:

- **`HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver`** (active) — resolves the
  OpenProject base URL from the configured `openproject.url` property, with an
  optional override via the `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` header when
  `openproject.allow-header-base-url` is `true`. The Bearer token is extracted
  from the `Authorization` header
  [HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java].
- **`EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver`** (disabled) — reads
  `OPENPROJECT_BASE_URL` and `OPENPROJECT_BEARER_TOKEN` from environment
  variables, intended for future STDIO transport support
  [EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java].

### Authorization Header Translation

`OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory` converts the MCP Bearer token into the OpenProject
expected format: `Basic base64("apikey:" + bearerToken)`
[OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory.java].

## Tool-Specific Behavior

### WorkPackageTools

The work package tools are the most complex, covering full CRUD plus attachments:

| Tool | HTTP Method | OpenProject API |
|------|------------|-----------------|
| `workPackageList` | GET | `/api/v3/projects/{id}/work_packages` |
| `workPackageShow` | GET | `/api/v3/work_packages/{id}` (404 → null) |
| `workPackageCreate` | POST | `/api/v3/projects/{id}/work_packages` |
| `workPackageUpdate` | PATCH | `/api/v3/work_packages/{id}` |
| `workPackageUploadAttachment` | POST (multipart) | `/api/v3/work_packages/{id}/attachments` |

`workPackageCreate` and `workPackageUpdate` use FreeMarker templates
(`create_work_package.ftl`, `update_work_package.ftl`) to render the JSON body
from a `PatchMap`, which conditionally includes null values based on the
`ALLOW_NULL_VALUES` flag
[OpenProjectApiClient][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java].

The `WorkPackageUpdateDto` extends `WorkPackageCreateDto` and adds a required
`lockVersion` field. The `@NotBlank` and `@NotNull` constraints on
`WorkPackageCreateDto` are overridden with `@JsonProperty` (no `required=true`)
in the subclass so that `subject` and `typeId` become optional during update
operations
[WorkPackageUpdateDto][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/dto/WorkPackageUpdateDto.java].

### RelationTools

The `relationList` tool merges four relation sources from the OpenProject API:
real relations from `_embedded.relations._embedded.elements`, the `parent` link
from `_links.parent`, `children` from `_links.children`, and `ancestors` from
`_links.ancestors`
[OpenProjectApiClient][src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java].

## Configuration Reference

Production configuration in [application.properties][src/main/resources/application.properties]:

| Property | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol` | `sse` | Transport protocol |
| `spring.ai.mcp.server.type` | `sync` | Execution model |
| `spring.ai.mcp.server.capabilities.tool` | `true` | Enable tool capabilities |
| `spring.ai.mcp.server.capabilities.prompt` | (default) | Enable prompt capabilities |
| `openproject.url` | `https://localhost` | OpenProject instance URL |
| `openproject.allow-header-base-url` | `false` | Allow per-request URL override |
| `spring.cache.type` | `caffeine` | Cache backend for token validation |
| `spring.cache.caffeine.spec` | `expireAfterWrite=60m,recordStats` | Token cache TTL |

## Testing

The test suite covers the MCP protocol layer through:

- **`McpToolsListIntegrationTest`** — verifies `tools/list` returns exactly 14
  tools with correct names, descriptions, and input schemas
  [McpToolsListIntegrationTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsListIntegrationTest.java].
- **`McpPromptsIntegrationTest`** — verifies `prompts/list` returns the expected
  prompts with correct names and descriptions
  [McpPromptsIntegrationTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpPromptsIntegrationTest.java].
- **`McpPingIntegrationTest`** — verifies `ping` returns valid JSON-RPC response
  [McpPingIntegrationTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpPingIntegrationTest.java].
- **`McpSecurityIntegrationTest`** — parameterized tests covering authentication
  scenarios: valid token, wrong token, missing token, and session ID validation
  [McpSecurityIntegrationTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpSecurityIntegrationTest.java].
- **Unit tests** for each tool class verify delegation to `OpenProjectApiClient`
  and constraint validation behavior
  [PriorityToolsTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/PriorityToolsTest.java],
  [ProjectToolsTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/ProjectToolsTest.java],
  [RelationToolsTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/RelationToolsTest.java],
  [TypesToolsTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/TypesToolsTest.java],
  [WorkPackageToolsTest][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/WorkPackageToolsTest.java].

Tests override the protocol to `STREAMABLE` to avoid open HTTP streams, and
import `McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig` to bypass authentication during testing
[McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig][src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig.java].

## Extension Points

- **Adding tools**: Create a `@Component` class in the `tools` package, annotate
  methods with `@McpTool`, and inject `OpenProjectApiClient` for data access.
  The annotation scanner auto-registers them.
- **Adding prompts**: Annotate a `@Component` method with `@McpPrompt` and
  `@McpArg` parameters. Return a `GetPromptResult` with `PromptMessage`s.
- **Changing connection resolution**: Swap `HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver`
  with `EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver` by activating the latter as a `@Component`
  and disabling the former.
- **Extending token validation**: Override `OpenProjectTokenValidator.fetchUserFromOpenProject()`
  to customize token validation logic (used in tests for stubbing).

nodes.title: Openproject client
nodes.body:
## Overview

The OpenProject REST Client subsystem provides a unified, Spring-managed bridge between the MCP server and the OpenProject REST API (v3). It spans seven collaborating components in the `de.tklein.tklab.openproject.mcp.openproject.client` package, plus a small set of Freemarker templates under `src/main/resources/templates/`.

At the top level, `OpenProjectApiClient` is the **public-facing service** (`@Service`) that tool classes (`WorkPackageTools`, `RelationTools`, `ProjectTools`, `TypesTools`, `PriorityTools`) call to create, read, update, and delete work packages and their metadata. The client delegates low-level HTTP transport to `OpenProjectRestOperations`, which in turn obtains a freshly-configured `RestClient` from `OpenProjectRestClientFactory` on every call. This design ensures that each HTTP request carries the **current** connection credentials, even in a multi-tenant scenario where different callers supply different bearer tokens.

## Connection Resolution

### OpenProjectConnection

A plain, immutable record (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectConnection.java`) holding two fields:

- `baseUrl` — the OpenProject instance URI (e.g. `https://openproject.example.com`)
- `bearerToken` — the raw API key / bearer token

No validation or transformation is performed at this layer; the record is a pure data carrier.

### OpenProjectConnectionResolver Interface

```java
public interface OpenProjectConnectionResolver {
  OpenProjectConnection resolve();
}
```

The interface is a single-method contract used by `OpenProjectRestClientFactory` and `OpenProjectTokenValidator` to obtain credentials at call time. Two concrete implementations exist:

| Implementation | Activation | Source of credentials |
|---|---|---|
| **HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver** | `@Component` (active by default) | `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` request header (if `openproject.allow-header-base-url=true`) or `openproject.url` fallback config; `Authorization: Bearer <token>` request header |
| **EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver** | `@Component` **disabled** (commented out) | `OPENPROJECT_BASE_URL` and `OPENPROJECT_BEARER_TOKEN` environment variables |

`HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java#L1-L60`) also uses `ObjectProvider<HttpServletRequest>` to lazily access the current request, returning `null` when no request context is available (e.g. during startup). When the header-based URL override is disabled (the default), the resolver always falls back to the Spring `@Value("${openproject.url}")` property.

### Integration-Test Override

The integration test `OpenProjectApiClientIntegrationTest` (`repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClientIntegrationTest.java#L95-L105`) provides a `@TestConfiguration` that registers a `@Primary` `OpenProjectConnectionResolver` bean returning a hardcoded `OpenProjectConnection` with the in-container OpenProject URL and a freshly generated admin API key. This ensures the test runs against the real OpenProject instance without depending on HTTP headers.

## RestClient Lifecycle and the Factory Pattern

`OpenProjectRestClientFactory` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestClientFactory.java`) is the bridge between the connection-resolver pattern and Spring's `RestClient`:

1. It calls `connectionResolver.resolve()` to obtain the current `OpenProjectConnection`.
2. It delegates `bearerToken` to `OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory` to produce the wire-format `Authorization` header.
3. It calls `restClientBuilder.clone()` to avoid mutating the shared `RestClient.Builder` bean, then sets `baseUrl` and the default `Authorization` header before building.

Every call to `OpenProjectRestOperations.op()` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L31-L33`) triggers a fresh `createClient()` invocation, meaning credentials are resolved **per-request**. This is the key mechanism that enables multi-tenant routing: each caller's token and base URL are picked up dynamically rather than at application startup.

### OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory

`OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory.java#L1-L18`) converts a bearer token into OpenProject's wire format:

```
Basic base64("apikey:" + bearerToken)
```

The factory validates that the token is non-blank, throwing `IllegalArgumentException` otherwise. The `"apikey:"` prefix is OpenProject's convention for API-key-based authentication; without it the server would treat the token as a password for a regular user account.

## Low-Level HTTP Operations

`OpenProjectRestOperations` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java`) exposes five HTTP methods, each delegating to the per-request `RestClient`:

| Method | HTTP verb | Content-Type | Accept | Return type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `getJson` | GET | — | `application/hal+json` | `JsonNode` |
| `postJson` | POST | `application/json` | `application/hal+json` | `JsonNode` |
| `patchJson` | PATCH | `application/json` | `application/hal+json` | `JsonNode` |
| `delete` | DELETE | — | `application/hal+json` | `void` (bodiless) |
| `postMultipart` | POST | `multipart/form-data` | `application/hal+json` | `JsonNode` |

All methods use Spring URI template expansion (`uri(String, Object...`) to substitute path variables. The `APPLICATION_HAL_JSON` constant is defined on the class itself (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L27`).

### Multipart Attachment Support

`buildMultipartAttachmentBody` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L90-L112`) constructs a `MultiValueMap` with two parts for OpenProject's attachment API:

1. **metadata** — a JSON entity (`{"fileName": "..."}`) with `Content-Type: application/json`
2. **file** — a `ByteArrayResource` with the original file's content type (or `application/octet-stream` as fallback)

This is used by `OpenProjectApiClient.workPackageUploadAttachment`.

### Embedded-Element Mapping Helper

`mapEmbeddedElements` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L105-L112`) navigates the HAL+JSON envelope to extract `_embedded.elements[]` and maps each node through a caller-supplied `Function<JsonNode, T>`. It returns an empty list when the result is null, not an array, or missing. All list-returning client methods (`workPackageList`, `typeList`, `priorityList`, `projectList`) use this helper.

## Freemarker Template Rendering

`OpenProjectTemplateRenderer` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectTemplateRenderer.java`) wraps FreeMarker's `Configuration` to render JSON payload templates into strings:

```java
public String render(String templateName, Map<String, ?> model)
```

The method catches `IOException` and `TemplateException` and wraps them in an `InternalError` with a descriptive message. Four templates are used in production:

| Template | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `create_work_package.ftl` | Full work-package creation payload with `_links` for type, priority, project, status, etc. |
| `update_work_package.ftl` | Partial update (PATCH) payload with conditional fields (`<#if ...??>`) and `lockVersion` |
| `create_parent_relation.ftl` | Relation creation payload with `type`, `description`, and `_links.to.href` |
| `update_parent_relation.ftl` | Parent-link update with `lockVersion` and conditional `parent.href` |

The templates use FreeMarker's `<#if ...??>` conditional syntax and `${...?json_string}` escaping to safely embed values into JSON. The `PatchMap` utility (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/util/PatchMap.java`) is used as the model builder, with `ALLOW_NULL_VALUES` to permit null entries to pass through (rather than being omitted).

## OpenProjectApiClient — High-Level Service

`OpenProjectApiClient` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java`) is the central service class. It depends on:

- `OpenProjectRestOperations` — HTTP transport
- `OpenProjectTemplateRenderer` — payload rendering
- Six mappers (`WorkPackageMapper`, `ProjectMapper`, `TypeMapper`, `PriorityMapper`, `RelationMapper`, `UserMapper`) — JSON-to-DTO conversion

### Key Responsibilities and Entry Points

| Method | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `root()` | Calls `GET /api/v3`, maps the root response through `UserMapper.fromRoot()` to identify the authenticated user. |
| `workPackageList(projectId)` | `GET /api/v3/projects/{projectId}/work_packages?pageSize=1000`; extracts `_embedded.elements` via `mapEmbeddedElements`. |
| `workPackageShow(wpId)` | `GET /api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}`; returns `null` on 404 (not an exception). |
| `workPackageCreate(projectId, dto)` | Builds a `PatchMap` model, renders `create_work_package.ftl`, `POST`s to `/api/v3/projects/{projectId}/work_packages`; returns the created work package's `id`. |
| `workPackageUpdate(wpId, dto)` | Builds a `PatchMap` model, renders `update_work_package.ftl`, `PATCH`es `/api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}`; returns `true` on success. |
| `workPackageUploadAttachment(wpId, fileName, content, contentType)` | Builds multipart body via `buildMultipartAttachmentBody`, `POST`s to `/api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}/attachments`; returns attachment `id`. |
| `typeList(projectId)` | `GET /api/v3/projects/{projectId}/types` |
| `priorityList()` | `GET /api/v3/priorities` |
| `projectList()` | `GET /api/v3/projects` |
| `listRelationsForWorkPackage(wpId)` | Complex multi-source relation extraction (see below). |
| `relationAdd(wpId, otherWpId, description, type)` | Renders `create_parent_relation.ftl`, `POST`s to `/api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}/relations`; returns `true` if the response has `id` and `_type`. |
| `relationDelete(relationId)` | `DELETE /api/v3/relations/{relationId}`; returns `false` on any exception (logs warning). |
| `relationAddParent(wpId, parentId)` | Reads `lockVersion` from the work package, renders `update_parent_relation.ftl`, `PATCH`es the work package with a parent link. |
| `relationDeleteParent(wpId)` | Like `relationAddParent` but sets `parentHref` to `null`. |

### Relation Extraction Strategy

`listRelationsForWorkPackage` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L142-L185`) aggregates relations from four distinct sources within a single work-package JSON response:

1. **Explicit relations** — `_embedded.relations._embedded.elements[]` (the HAL+JSON nested resource array). Mapped via `RelationMapper.fromRelationElement()`.
2. **Parent link** — `_links.parent` (derived from HAL links). Mapped via `RelationMapper.fromWpLink("parent", ...)`.
3. **Children links** — `_links.children[]` array. Each element mapped as a "children" relation.
4. **Ancestors links** — `_links.ancestors[]` array. Each element mapped as an "ancestors" relation.

Results are filtered to exclude entries where `toId`, `to`, and `id` are all null. This four-source approach is necessary because the OpenProject HAL+JSON response embeds explicit relations in `_embedded` but encodes parent/children/ancestors as `_links` entries rather than embedded resources.

### Failure Semantics

| Scenario | Behavior |
|---|---|
| 404 on `workPackageShow` | Returns `null` (not an exception). |
| 404 on `workPackageList` / non-existent project | Propagates `RestClientResponseException` (404). |
| 422 on `relationAdd` with invalid IDs | Propagates `HttpClientErrorException` (422). |
| `relationDelete` on non-existent relation | Returns `false` (logs warning); does not propagate. |
| Freemarker template failure | Throws `InternalError` wrapping the original `IOException`/`TemplateException`. |

## Security Integration

`OpenProjectTokenValidator` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java`) depends on both `OpenProjectConnectionResolver` and `OpenProjectApiClient`. Its `validateCurrentRequestOrThrow()` method:

1. Resolves the current connection via `connectionResolver.resolve()`.
2. Validates that `baseUrl` and `bearerToken` are non-blank.
3. Hashes `baseUrl + "|" + token` with SHA-256 to produce a cache key (the raw token is never stored).
4. Calls the `cachedCheckToken` supplier, which invokes `openProjectApiClient.root()` to verify the token against the OpenProject server.
5. Caches the result (`ValidatedOpenProjectUser`) keyed by the hashed token.

`McpBearerAuthenticationFilter` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java`) is a Spring `OncePerRequestFilter` that:

- Filters only MCP endpoints (`/sse`, `/mcp`, `/mcp/*`).
- Calls `tokenValidator.validateCurrentRequestOrThrow()` on every request.
- Sets a `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` with `ROLE_MCP_USER` into `SecurityContextHolder`.
- Persists the security context to a `RequestAttributeSecurityContextRepository` so it survives async dispatch (required for SSE).
- On `UnauthorizedException`, clears the context and returns HTTP 401 with `{"error":"unauthorized"}`.

`fetchUserFromOpenProject()` in `OpenProjectTokenValidator` is a template method that `OpenProjectApiClient.root()` calls. Tests can override it to avoid real network calls while preserving caching behavior.

## Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph MCP Server
    WP[WorkPackageTools]
    RT[RelationTools]
    PT[ProjectTools]
    TT[TypesTools]
    PrT[PriorityTools]
    AF[McpBearerAuthenticationFilter]
  end

  subgraph "client package"
    OP[OpenProjectApiClient]
    RO[OpenProjectRestOperations]
    RF[OpenProjectRestClientFactory]
    CR[OpenProjectConnectionResolver]
    AH[OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory]
    TR[OpenProjectTemplateRenderer]
  end

  subgraph "security package"
    TV[OpenProjectTokenValidator]
  end

  subgraph "templates"
    TW[create_work_package.ftl]
    TU[update_work_package.ftl]
    CP[create_parent_relation.ftl]
    UP[update_parent_relation.ftl]
  end

  WP --> OP
  RT --> OP
  PT --> OP
  TT --> OP
  PrT --> OP
  AF --> TV

  OP --> RO
  OP --> TR
  OP --> TM[TypeMapper]
  OP --> PM[ProjectMapper]
  OP --> WM[WorkPackageMapper]
  OP --> PrM[PriorityMapper]
  OP --> RM[RelationMapper]
  OP --> UM[UserMapper]

  RO --> RF
  TR --> FT[FreeMarker Configuration]

  RF --> CR
  RF --> AH

  TV --> CR
  TV --> OP
```

## Configuration

| Property | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `openproject.url` | *(required)* | Fallback base URL for the OpenProject instance |
| `openproject.allow-header-base-url` | `false` | When `true`, allows `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` header to override the configured URL per-request |

The `HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver` reads these via `@Value` injection. The `OPENPROJECT_BASE_URL` and `OPENPROJECT_BEARER_TOKEN` environment variables are read by the disabled `EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver`.

## Extension Points

- **New connection resolvers**: Implement `OpenProjectConnectionResolver` and register as a `@Component`. If multiple beans exist, mark one `@Primary` or use `ObjectProvider` injection to disambiguate.
- **Template rendering**: The `OpenProjectTemplateRenderer` is injected with a Spring `Configuration` bean. New templates can be added to `src/main/resources/templates/` without code changes if they follow the existing `PatchMap` model contract.
- **Token validation**: `OpenProjectTokenValidator.fetchUserFromOpenProject()` is a template method; subclasses can override it to use a different validation mechanism (e.g., introspection endpoint).
- **REST operations**: `OpenProjectRestOperations` could be extended with additional HTTP methods (e.g., PUT, HEAD) or content types as needed.

## Testing

The integration test `OpenProjectApiClientIntegrationTest` (`repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClientIntegrationTest.java`) covers:

- Container lifecycle (docker compose up/down with configurable tag, port, shutdown)
- `root()` authentication
- `projectList()` with demo project detection
- `workPackageShow` returning `null` for non-existent IDs
- `relationDelete` returning `false` for non-existent relations
- `workPackageList` throwing 404 for non-existent projects
- `priorityList` and `typeList` returning non-empty lists with IDs and names
- Full CRUD cycle: create work package, list, show, update subject, upload attachment, add/delete relation, add/delete parent relation

The test configures a `@Primary` `OpenProjectConnectionResolver` bean that returns hardcoded credentials, and it starts a real OpenProject container to validate against the actual API.

nodes.body:
# System Overview

The Spring OpenProject MCP Server is a Java application that exposes an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (Model Context Protocol) server for managing OpenProject work packages. It acts as a thin proxy between an MCP-compatible client (e.g., an LLM agent) and the OpenProject REST API (`/api/v3`), translating MCP tool calls into authenticated HTTP requests and returning structured results as JSON.

## Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client["MCP Client (e.g., LM Studio)"]
        C["LLM Agent"]
    end

    subgraph Server["Spring OpenProject MCP Server"]
        subgraph Transport["MCP Transport"]
            SSE["SSE /streamable HTTP"]
        end
        subgraph Security["Security Layer"]
            Filter["McpBearerAuthenticationFilter"]
            Validator["OpenProjectTokenValidator"]
            Cache["OpenProjectTokenValidationCache\n(Caffeine, 60m TTL)"]
        end
        subgraph Tools["MCP Tool Beans"]
            WP["WorkPackageTools"]
            PR["ProjectTools"]
            PT["PriorityTools"]
            RT["RelationTools"]
            TY["TypesTools"]
            CM["Common"]
        end
        subgraph ClientLayer["OpenProject Client Layer"]
            ApiClient["OpenProjectApiClient"]
            RestOps["OpenProjectRestOperations"]
            RestClient["RestClient (per-request auth)"]
        end
        subgraph Mapping["Mapping & Rendering"]
            Mappers["MapStruct DTO Mappers"]
            FTL["FreeMarker Templates"]
        end
    end

    C -->|JSON-RPC over SSE| SSE
    SSE --> Filter
    Filter --> Validator
    Validator --> Cache
    Validator -->|validate token| ApiClient
    Filter --> Tools
    Tools --> ApiClient
    ApiClient --> RestOps
    RestOps --> RestClient
    RestClient -->|HTTP| OP["OpenProject API"]
    ApiClient --> Mappers
    ApiClient --> FTL
```

*Figure 1: High-level component architecture and request flow.*

## Core Components

### Entry Point

The application is a standard Spring Boot 4.1.1 application with `SpringOpenprojectMcpServerApplication` as its `@SpringBootApplication` entry point (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/SpringOpenprojectMcpServerApplication.java`). It runs on port `8080` with a separate management port at `8081`.

### MCP Transport

The server uses Spring AI's MCP server starter (`spring-ai-starter-mcp-server`) with the `webmvc` transport (`spring-ai-starter-mcp-server-webmvc`). The protocol is configurable via `spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol`:

- **SSE** (`spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol=sse`): Exposes `GET /sse` for server-to-client streaming and `POST /mcp` for client-to-server JSON-RPC messages.
- **STREAMABLE**: Exposes a single bidirectional endpoint at `/mcp` based on the MCP streamable HTTP spec.

The two protocols cannot be bound simultaneously because the transport defines the wiring, endpoints, and message routing. The default is SSE.

Configuration is in `repo://src/main/resources/application.properties`:
- `spring.ai.mcp.server.name=openproject-mcp-server`
- `spring.ai.mcp.server.version=1.2.0`
- `spring.ai.mcp.server.type=sync`
- `spring.ai.mcp.server.capabilities.tool=true`
- `spring.ai.mcp.server.annotation-scanner.enabled=true`

### Security Model

Authentication uses a two-layer approach:

1. **MCP-level authentication**: The `McpBearerAuthenticationFilter` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java`) intercepts requests to `/mcp` and `/sse` paths, extracts the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, and validates the token against OpenProject.

2. **OpenProject API authentication**: The validated bearer token is converted to OpenProject's expected `Basic` auth format (`apikey:<token>`) by `OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory.java`), which then serves as the `Authorization` header for all outbound HTTP requests to the OpenProject REST API.

Token validation uses `OpenProjectTokenValidator` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java`), which calls `OpenProjectApiClient.root()` (the `/api/v3` endpoint) to verify the token. Validated user info (`href`, `name`) is cached in a Caffeine-backed `@Cacheable` store (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidationCache.java`) with a 60-minute TTL. The raw token is never stored in the cache; only its SHA-256 hash serves as the cache key.

The `OpenProjectConnectionResolver` interface (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectConnectionResolver.java`) abstracts how the OpenProject base URL and bearer token are obtained. The active implementation is `HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java`), which reads the base URL from:
- The configured `openproject.url` property (default `https://localhost`), or
- The `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` header when `openproject.allow-header-base-url=true` is set.

A secondary `EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java`) exists but is commented out, providing an environment-variable-based alternative (`OPENPROJECT_BASE_URL`, `OPENPROJECT_BEARER_TOKEN`).

Spring Security configures two filter chains in `SecurityConfig` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java`):
- **Actuator chain** (`@Order(1)`): Protects `/actuator/**` with HTTP Basic auth for an admin user. Health endpoints are publicly accessible.
- **MCP chain** (`@Order(2)`): Protects `/mcp/**`, `/mcp`, `/error`, and `/sse` with bearer-based authentication via the custom filter. CSRF is disabled.

The `McpBearerAuthenticationFilter` is explicitly registered inside the Spring Security chain (not as a global servlet filter) via a `FilterRegistrationBean` with `setEnabled(false)`.

### MCP Tools

The server exposes five tool beans and one logging handler, each annotated with `@McpTool`, `@McpPrompt`, or `@McpLogging`:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `WorkPackageTools` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/WorkPackageTools.java`) | Query, create, update work packages; upload attachments; provides a `safe_edit` prompt for diff-based safe editing with lockVersion concurrency control. |
| `ProjectTools` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/ProjectTools.java`) | List visible projects; provides a `project.summary` prompt generator. |
| `PriorityTools` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/PriorityTools.java`) | List available priorities. |
| `RelationTools` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/RelationTools.java`) | List/add/delete work package relations (relates, blocks, precedes, duplicates, includes, requires); manage parent/child hierarchy. |
| `TypesTools` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/TypesTools.java`) | List allowed work package types for a project. |
| `Common` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/Common.java`) | Handles MCP `logging/message` notifications, forwarding them to application log. |

All tools are `@Component` beans with constructor injection of `OpenProjectApiClient`. The `@Validated` annotation on tools enables Jakarta Bean Validation for tool parameters.

### OpenProject Client Layer

`OpenProjectApiClient` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java`) is the central service that translates MCP tool operations into OpenProject REST API calls. It:

- Delegates HTTP requests to `OpenProjectRestOperations` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java`), which creates a per-request `RestClient` via `OpenProjectRestClientFactory` (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestClientFactory.java`). Each request gets a fresh client with the current connection's base URL and auth header.
- Uses `application/hal+json` as the content type for all API communication.
- Supports GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, and multipart POST operations.

For write operations (create work package, update work package, add parent relation), the client uses FreeMarker templates (`repo://src/main/resources/templates/`) to generate the JSON request bodies. This approach avoids the brittleness of a generated OpenAPI client (noted in the README) while maintaining compatibility across OpenProject 14, 15, 16.6, and 17.7. The templates are:
- `create_work_package.ftl`
- `update_work_package.ftl`
- `create_parent_relation.ftl`
- `update_parent_relation.ftl`

The `PatchMap` utility (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/util/PatchMap.java`) provides a fluent API for building maps with optional null-value filtering, used to populate template models with only the fields that have non-null values.

### DTOs and Mappers

The system defines domain-specific DTOs (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/dto/`) for all OpenProject entities:

- `WorkPackageDto` — work package fields (id, subject, description, dates, story points, type, priority, etc.)
- `WorkPackageCreateDto` — validation groups (`OnCreate`) for required fields on creation
- `WorkPackageUpdateDto` — extends `WorkPackageCreateDto` with `lockVersion` for optimistic locking
- `ProjectDto` — project metadata
- `PriorityDto`, `TypeDto`, `RelationDto`, `RelationValuesDto`, `UserDto`

MapStruct mappers (`repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/mapper/`) convert between `JsonNode` (raw API responses) and DTOs. They use default methods for custom mapping logic (e.g., extracting nested paths, parsing date strings, handling missing nodes). The mappers are registered as Spring beans via `@Mapper(componentModel = "spring")`.

### Request Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant SSE
    participant Filter
    participant Validator
    participant Cache
    participant Tool
    participant ApiClient
    participant OP

    Client->>SSE: JSON-RPC (tool call)
    SSE->>Filter: doFilter()
    Filter->>Validator: validateCurrentRequestOrThrow()
    Validator->>Cache: cachedCheckToken(key)
    alt cache hit
        Cache-->>Validator: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    else cache miss
        Validator->>Validator: sha256Hex(baseUrl|token)
        Validator->>OP: GET /api/v3 (auth check)
        OP-->>Validator: UserDto
        Validator->>Cache: store(60m TTL)
        Cache-->>Validator: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    end
    Validator-->>Filter: auth success
    Filter->>Filter: set SecurityContext
    Filter->>Tool: dispatch tool call
    Tool->>ApiClient: workPackageList(projectId)
    ApiClient->>OP: GET /api/v3/projects/...
    OP-->>ApiClient: JsonNode (HAL+JSON)
    ApiClient->>ApiClient: mapEmbeddedElements()
    ApiClient-->>Tool: List<WorkPackageDto>
    Tool-->>Client: JSON result
```

*Figure 2: Request lifecycle from MCP client through auth to OpenProject API.*

### Configuration

Key configuration properties in `repo://src/main/resources/application.properties`:

| Property | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol` | `sse` | Transport protocol (sse or streamable) |
| `openproject.url` | `https://localhost` | Default OpenProject base URL |
| `openproject.allow-header-base-url` | `false` | Allow per-request URL override via `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` header |
| `spring.cache.type` | `caffeine` | Cache provider |
| `spring.cache.caffeine.spec` | `expireAfterWrite=60m,recordStats` | Auth validation cache spec |
| `management.server.port` | `8081` | Actuator management port |

Environment variable `OPENPROJECT_ALLOW_HEADER_BASE_URL=true` enables the header-based URL override at the container level.

### Extension Points

1. **Connection resolver**: Replace `HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver` with a custom `OpenProjectConnectionResolver` implementation (e.g., `EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver` or a new one) to change how the OpenProject URL and bearer token are resolved.

2. **Token validator**: Override `fetchUserFromOpenProject()` in `OpenProjectTokenValidator` (as done in tests) to customize token validation logic without affecting caching or keying behavior.

3. **MCP tools**: Add new `@McpTool`-annotated `@Component` beans to expose additional MCP tools. The annotation scanner auto-discovers them.

4. **FreeMarker templates**: Extend or modify the four `.ftl` templates to change the JSON structure sent to the OpenProject API.

5. **MapStruct mappers**: Add new `@Mapper` interfaces for new DTO types.

### Testing

Tests are in `repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/`:

- **Integration tests** (`@Tag(TAG_INTEGRATION_TEST_LOCAL)`): Run against a real OpenProject Docker container (`mvn test -Dopenproject.container.tag=17.5.1`). Includes `OpenProjectApiClientIntegrationTest`.
- **MCP protocol tests**: `McpToolsListIntegrationTest`, `McpPromptsIntegrationTest`, `McpPingIntegrationTest` verify MCP tool discovery, prompt generation, and ping responses via raw HTTP against a random-port server.
- **Security tests**: `McpSecurityIntegrationTest` parameterizes auth scenarios (valid/invalid/missing tokens) across `initialize`, tools/list, and ping endpoints.
- **Unit tests**: `WorkPackageToolsTest`, `ProjectToolsTest`, `RelationToolsTest`, `PriorityToolsTest`, `TypesToolsTest`, `PatchMapTest` test individual components.
- `McpToolsHelper` provides shared HTTP client code for MCP protocol testing.

### Operational Notes

- The Docker image runs on port `8080`; the `--tmpfs /tmp` mount prevents temp file leakage between container restarts.
- The API token is passed per-MCP-request via the `Authorization` header and never persisted in the container.
- Actuator admin credentials are configured via `actuator.security.admin.username` and `actuator.security.admin.password-hash` (bcrypt-prefixed).
- OTel tracing, logging, and metrics are all disabled by default.
- The `spring-openproject-mcp-server` is licensed under MIT.

# Security Architecture

This page documents the authentication and authorization layer of the OpenProject MCP server. The system validates incoming MCP requests against an external OpenProject instance using bearer tokens, caches validation results with Caffeine, and supports multi-tenant scenarios where each request can target a different OpenProject deployment.

## Spring Security Filter Chains

`SecurityConfig` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java)) defines two `SecurityFilterChain` beans, distinguished by `@Order` and `securityMatcher` path predicates.

### Actuator Chain (Order 1)

- **Path predicate:** `/actuator/**`
- **Auth mechanism:** HTTP Basic authentication
- **Authorization:** Only `/actuator/health` and `/actuator/health/*` are permitted without credentials. All other actuator endpoints require the `ACTUATOR_ADMIN` role.
- **CSRF:** Disabled
- **User store:** `InMemoryUserDetailsManager` configured from `actuator.security.admin.username` and `actuator.security.admin.password-hash` properties. The password hash must include an `{id}` prefix (e.g. `{bcrypt}...`).

The actuator chain is evaluated first because of `@Order(1)`. It provides health-check access and protects all other Spring Boot Actuator endpoints with basic auth.

### MCP Chain (Order 2)

- **Path predicate:** `/mcp/**`, `/mcp`, `/error`, `/sse`
- **Auth mechanism:** Bearer token (no HTTP Basic)
- **Authorization:** All requests require authentication (`anyRequest().authenticated()`)
- **CSRF:** Disabled
- **HTTP Basic:** Explicitly disabled

The MCP filter (`McpBearerAuthenticationFilter`, a `@Component`) is **not** registered as a global servlet filter. `SecurityConfig` creates a `FilterRegistrationBean<McpBearerAuthenticationFilter>` with `setEnabled(false)` to suppress the automatic registration. Instead, the filter is injected explicitly into the MCP chain via `addFilterBefore(mcpFilter, UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter.class)`, so it runs inside the Spring Security filter pipeline.

## Bearer Token Validation Flow

The validation of each incoming MCP request follows a well-defined pipeline:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Filter as McpBearerAuthenticationFilter
    participant Validator as OpenProjectTokenValidator
    participant Cache as OpenProjectTokenValidationCache
    participant Resolver as OpenProjectConnectionResolver
    participant OpenProject

    Client->>Filter: HTTP request with Authorization: Bearer <token>
    Filter->>Filter: shouldNotFilter() -- path matches /mcp or /sse?
    Filter->>Validator: validateCurrentRequestOrThrow()
    Validator->>Resolver: resolve()
    Resolver-->>Validator: OpenProjectConnection(baseUrl, bearerToken)
    Validator->>Validator: SHA-256 hash of baseUrl|bearerToken
    Validator->>Cache: cachedCheckToken(key, supplier)
    alt cache hit
        Cache-->>Validator: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    else cache miss
        Cache->>Validator: invoke supplier
        Validator->>OpenProject: GET /api/v3 (root)
        OpenProject-->>Validator: UserDto
        Validator->>Cache: store ValidatedOpenProjectUser
        Cache-->>Validator: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    end
    Validator-->>Filter: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    Filter->>Filter: create UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken
    Filter->>Filter: set authentication in SecurityContextHolder
    Filter->>Filter: save SecurityContext to request attribute
    Filter->>Client: pass request down the chain
```

### Step 1: Connection Resolution

`OpenProjectConnectionResolver` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectConnectionResolver.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectConnectionResolver.java)) is the interface that abstracts where OpenProject connection details come from. Two implementations exist:

1. **`HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver`** -- The active, production resolver. It reads the `Authorization` header from the current `HttpServletRequest` (via `ObjectProvider<HttpServletRequest>`) to extract the bearer token, and optionally reads `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` for multi-tenant URL override.

2. **`EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver`** -- A commented-out (`// @Component`) resolver that reads `OPENPROJECT_BASE_URL` and `OPENPROJECT_BEARER_TOKEN` from environment variables. It is intended for a future STDIO-based deployment mode.

### Step 2: Token Keying and Caching

`OpenProjectTokenValidator` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java)) constructs a cache key by concatenating `baseUrl|bearerToken` and computing a SHA-256 hex digest (`DigestUtils.sha256Hex`). The raw token is **never** stored in the cache.

The cache lookup uses Spring's `@Cacheable` annotation on `OpenProjectTokenValidationCache.cachedCheckToken()` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidationCache.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidationCache.java)). The cache name is `auth-validation`, configured in `application.properties` ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties)) as:

```properties
spring.cache.type=caffeine
spring.cache.cache-names=auth-validation
spring.cache.caffeine.spec=expireAfterWrite=60m,recordStats
```

On a cache miss, the method invokes a `Supplier<ValidatedOpenProjectUser>` that calls `fetchUserFromOpenProject()` (a template method) to perform the actual API call. The result is stored in the Caffeine cache with a 60-minute write expiry and stats recording enabled.

### Step 3: OpenProject API Validation

The token validation call goes through `OpenProjectApiClient.root()` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java)), which performs `GET /api/v3`. The HTTP client is built by `OpenProjectRestClientFactory` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestClientFactory.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestClientFactory.java)), which uses `OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory.java)) to convert the bearer token into OpenProject's expected `Basic` auth header format (`Basic base64("apikey:<token>")`).

The `root()` call returns a `UserDto`. If the response is `null`, the `href` is `null` or blank, or any `RestClientResponseException` occurs, `UnauthorizedException` is thrown.

### Step 4: Security Context Establishment

`McpBearerAuthenticationFilter` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java)) wraps the validated user in a `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` with a single `ROLE_MCP_USER` authority, sets it on `SecurityContextHolder`, and persists the context to a request attribute via `RequestAttributeSecurityContextRepository`. This attribute-based persistence is critical for Spring Security to restore the context during the async dispatches used by the SSE protocol.

If validation fails, the filter clears `SecurityContextHolder`, sets HTTP 401 status, and writes `{"error":"unauthorized"}` as `application/json`.

## Multi-Tenant Connection Resolution

`HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java)) enables each MCP request to target a different OpenProject instance:

- **Base URL:** Read from `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` header when `openproject.allow-header-base-url=true`. Falls back to the `openproject.url` property.
- **Bearer token:** Extracted from the `Authorization` header (prefix `Bearer ` stripped).
- **Configuration:** `openproject.allow-header-base-url` defaults to `false` in `application.properties`.

The resolver always returns an `OpenProjectConnection` record ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectConnection.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectConnection.java)) containing the `baseUrl` URI and `bearerToken` string.

## Token Cache Invalidation

The Caffeine cache uses `expireAfterWrite=60m` with no explicit eviction policy beyond TTL. Tokens are never removed from the cache by invalidation logic -- a token that was valid at validation time remains cached for 60 minutes even if the user is later disabled or the token is revoked in OpenProject. This is a design trade-off favoring latency over strict real-time revocation.

## Security Context Repository

The filter uses `RequestAttributeSecurityContextRepository` (the default for servlet-based Spring Security) to persist the `SecurityContext`. This is essential because the MCP SSE protocol uses async dispatches: the original HTTP request completes after the SSE connection is established, and subsequent messages arrive as separate async dispatches. Without the attribute-based persistence, the context would be lost between dispatches.

The filter overrides `shouldNotFilterAsyncDispatch()` to return `false`, ensuring it runs on every async dispatch and re-validates the security context.

## Error Handling

`UnauthorizedException` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/UnauthorizedException.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/UnauthorizedException.java)) is an unchecked `RuntimeException` used throughout the validation pipeline. The filter catches it in `doFilterInternal` and translates it to an HTTP 401 response with a JSON body. Any other exception during validation propagates up the filter chain and results in a 500 error.

## Configuration Properties

| Property | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `openproject.url` | `https://localhost` | Fallback base URL for OpenProject API |
| `openproject.allow-header-base-url` | `false` | Enable per-request URL override via header |
| `actuator.security.admin.username` | `admin` | Actuator admin username |
| `actuator.security.admin.password-hash` | (required) | bcrypt-prefixed password hash for actuator admin |

## Tests

`McpSecurityIntegrationTest` ([repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpSecurityIntegrationTest.java](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpSecurityIntegrationTest.java)) validates the authentication flow end-to-end using a `@SpringBootTest` with a random port. It provides a stub `OpenProjectTokenValidator` via a `@TestConfiguration` that accepts a `VALID_TOKEN` ("correctToken") and rejects all others. The test covers:

- `initializeMcp` (MCP initialization) with valid/invalid/missing tokens
- `callToolsListRequest` with and without prior initialization
- `callPingRequest` with and without prior initialization
- `callPromptsListRequest` with and without prior initialization

Each scenario is parameterized with `@CsvSource` asserting the expected HTTP status code (200 for valid, 401 for invalid/missing, 404 for missing session).

## `ValidatedOpenProjectUser`

`ValidatedOpenProjectUser` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/ValidatedOpenProjectUser.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/ValidatedOpenProjectUser.java)) is a simple record holding the user's `href` (from the OpenProject user link) and `name`. It is the cache entry type and is stored as the principal in the `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken`. Its minimal structure means the cache stores only lightweight data -- the full `UserDto` is not retained.

nodes.title: Configuration and Profiles
nodes.description: Spring Boot profile system (dev, local, prod, test) for the OpenProject MCP server, including application properties, environment variables, MCP server protocol selection (SSE vs STREAMABLE), and deployment-time profile activation.
nodes.body:
This page describes the configuration model for the OpenProject MCP Server, a Spring Boot application built on Spring AI's MCP server starter. Profiles control environment-specific behavior such as logging levels, OpenProject connection targets, health probes, and the MCP transport protocol.

## Profile Overview

The project defines five Spring Boot profile property files:

| Profile | File | Purpose |
|---------|------|---------|
| `base` (no profile) | `repo://src/main/resources/application.properties` | Default configuration shared by all environments |
| `dev` | `repo://src/main/resources/application-dev.properties` | Developer workstation debugging |
| `local` | `repo://src/main/resources/application-local.properties` | Local integration against a specific OpenProject instance |
| `prod` | `repo://src/main/resources/application-prod.properties` | Production deployment (default for Docker) |
| `test` | `repo://src/test/resources/application-test.properties` | Container-based integration tests |

Profiles are **not** activated by `spring.profiles.active` inside any properties file. Instead, activation is controlled externally:

- **Docker deployment** activates `prod` via JVM argument: `java -Dspring.profiles.active=prod -jar /app/app.jar` ([repo://docker/Dockerfile#L29](repo://docker/Dockerfile#L29))
- **IDE / local runs** activate a profile via IDE run configuration, command-line `--spring.profiles.active=dev`, or the `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` environment variable.
- **Tests** use `@SpringBootTest` with `properties = { ... }` to override individual settings rather than activating a profile file.

The Maven build excludes all `application-*.properties` from the JAR ([repo://pom.xml#L278-L281](repo://pom.xml#L278-L281)). At Docker image build time, `application-prod.properties` is copied separately into the image root ([repo://docker/Dockerfile#L13](repo://docker/Dockerfile#L13)), so the production profile's overrides are available at runtime.

## Base Configuration (No Profile)

`application.properties` establishes the application's defaults:

- **Application identity**: `spring.application.name=spring-openproject-mcp-server`
- **Server**: HTTP on `0.0.0.0:8080`; management (actuator) on port `8081`
- **Caching**: Caffeine cache named `auth-validation`, evicting after 60 minutes of inactivity with stats recording ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L6-L8](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L6-L8))
- **OTLP observability**: Tracing, logging, and metrics export are all **disabled** by default ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L10-L12](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L10-L12))
- **MCP server** ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L14-L20](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L14-L20)):
  - Enabled (`spring.ai.mcp.server.enabled=true`)
  - Name: `openproject-mcp-server`, version `1.2.0`
  - **Protocol: `sse`** (Server-Sent Events) — the default transport
  - Tool capability enabled (`spring.ai.mcp.server.capabilities.tool=true`)
  - Type: `sync` (synchronous server)
  - Annotation scanner enabled
- **OpenProject connection**: Default URL is `https://localhost`; header-based base URL override is **disabled** (`openproject.allow-header-base-url=false`)
- **Actuator security**: Admin username `admin` with a placeholder bcrypt password hash; endpoints are **disabled** by default (`endpoints.enabled=false`)

## Profile-Specific Overrides

### `dev` Profile

`application-dev.properties` ([repo://src/main/resources/application-dev.properties](repo://src/main/resources/application-dev.properties)):

- Sets `logging.level.org.springframework.ai=DEBUG` and `logging.level.io.modelcontextprotocol=DEBUG` for verbose AI/MCP debugging.
- Disables Spring DevTools restart (`spring.devtools.restart.enabled=false`) to avoid interference with the MCP server's long-running SSE connections.

This profile is intended for developers running the app locally in an IDE who need visibility into Spring AI and MCP protocol traffic.

### `local` Profile

`application-local.properties` ([repo://src/main/resources/application-local.properties](repo://src/main/resources/application-local.properties)):

- Overrides `openproject.url=https://pro.t-klein.de` to target a specific OpenProject instance.
- Enables `TRACE` logging for the OpenProject client package (`de.tklein.tklab.openproject.mcp.openproject.client`) for deep HTTP debugging.

This profile is for a developer's personal integration environment pointing at a known OpenProject deployment.

### `prod` Profile

`application-prod.properties` ([repo://src/main/resources/application-prod.properties](repo://src/main/resources/application-prod.properties)):

- Reduces logging: `ERROR` for Spring framework, `INFO` for the application package.
- Hides the Spring banner (`spring.main.banner-mode=off`).
- Exposes only the `/actuator/health` endpoint at base path `/actuator`.
- Disables detailed health output (`show-details=never`, `show-components=never`).
- Enables Kubernetes-style readiness/liveness probes (`management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true`).
- Disables disk space and SSL health checks (`management.health.diskspace.enabled=false`, `management.health.ssl.enabled=false`).

This profile is the **only** one bundled into the Docker image and is activated automatically at container start.

### `test` Profile

`application-test.properties` ([repo://src/test/resources/application-test.properties](repo://src/test/resources/application-test.properties)):

- Sets the OpenProject container image tag to `17.7.2` (`openproject.container.tag`).
- Disables automatic container shutdown (`openproject.container.shutdown=false`).
- Configures the container port to `18088` (`openproject.container.port`).
- Explicitly sets `openproject.allow-header-base-url=false`.

This profile supports integration tests that spin up a real OpenProject container to validate end-to-end MCP tool behavior.

## MCP Server Protocol Selection

The MCP server supports two transport protocols:

| Protocol | Property | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `sse` (default) | `spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol=sse` | Server-Sent Events. The server maintains a persistent SSE connection to stream messages to the client. Default in production. |
| `STREAMABLE` | `spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol=STREAMABLE` | HTTP-based streamable transport. Each request is a discrete HTTP call with optional continuation. No persistent connection. |

The base configuration defaults to `sse` ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L18](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L18)). The `prod` profile does not override this, so production deployments use SSE.

Integration tests override the protocol to `STREAMABLE` at the test level ([repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpPingIntegrationTest.java#L22](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpPingIntegrationTest.java#L22), [repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpSecurityIntegrationTest.java#L28](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpSecurityIntegrationTest.java#L28), [repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsListIntegrationTest.java#L29](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsListIntegrationTest.java#L29), [repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpPromptsIntegrationTest.java#L26](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpPromptsIntegrationTest.java#L26)). The test comments explain that `STREAMABLE` is preferred in tests because it avoids leaving an open SSE stream during test teardown.

## Configuration Injection Points

Configuration values are consumed by the application through Spring's `@Value` injection:

- **`openproject.allow-header-base-url`** — controls whether the `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` HTTP header is trusted to override the base URL. Injected in `HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java#L24](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java#L24)).
- **`actuator.security.admin.username`** and **`actuator.security.admin.password-hash`** — secure the actuator endpoint. Injected in `SecurityConfig` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L32-L33](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L32-L33)).

## Deployment Configuration

The Docker image ([repo://docker/Dockerfile](repo://docker/Dockerfile)) packages the application as follows:

1. Base image: Eclipse Temurin JRE (JDK 25).
2. Copies the application JAR as `app.jar`.
3. Copies `application-prod.properties` to the image root (not inside `BOOT-INF/classes`).
4. Runs as a non-root `spring` user.
5. Activates the `prod` profile via `-Dspring.profiles.active=prod`.
6. Exposes port `8080` (HTTP) and `8081` (actuator).
7. Health check queries the actuator readiness endpoint on port `8081`.

The production profile's health probe configuration (`management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true`) enables Kubernetes-style `/actuator/health/liveness` and `/actuator/health/readiness` endpoints, which the Docker `HEALTHCHECK` directive queries.
