nodes.body:
# DTOs and Mappers This page describes the data transfer object (DTO) types and their corresponding `JsonNode` → DTO mapper interfaces that bridge the OpenProject REST API's JSON wire format to typed Java objects inside the MCP server. ## Architecture All DTOs live in the `de.tklein.tklab.openproject.mcp.dto` package. All mappers live in `de.tklein.tklab.openproject.mcp.mapper`. The sole consumer of every mapper is the `OpenProjectApiClient` service (`OpenProjectApiClient`), which receives all mappers via constructor injection and applies them to JSON responses returned by the OpenProject REST API. ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "OpenProject REST API" API["JSON responses"] end subgraph "MCP Server" Client["OpenProjectApiClient
(@Service)"] subgraph "Mappers" PrioMapper["PriorityMapper"] ProjMapper["ProjectMapper"] TypeMapper["TypeMapper"] UserMapper["UserMapper"] RelMapper["RelationMapper"] WPMapper["WorkPackageMapper"] end subgraph "DTOs" PrioDto["PriorityDto"] ProjDto["ProjectDto"] TypeDto["TypeDto"] UserDto["UserDto"] RelDto["RelationDto"] RelValsDto["RelationValuesDto"] WPDto["WorkPackageDto"] WPCreateDto["WorkPackageCreateDto"] WPUpdateDto["WorkPackageUpdateDto"] end end API --> Client Client --> PrioMapper Client --> ProjMapper Client --> TypeMapper Client --> UserMapper Client --> RelMapper Client --> WPMapper PrioMapper --> PrioDto ProjMapper --> ProjDto TypeMapper --> TypeDto UserMapper --> UserDto RelMapper --> RelDto RelMapper --> RelValsDto WPMapper --> WPDto WPMapper --> WPCreateDto WPMapper --> WPUpdateDto ``` ## DTOs ### PriorityDto Represents a single priority from the OpenProject API (`/api/v3/priorities/{id}`). Fields: `id`, `name`, `position`, `href`. `position` may be `null` when the API omits it. ### ProjectDto Represents a project from the OpenProject API. Fields: `id`, `identifier`, `name`, `active`, `isPublic`, `status`, `description`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `href`. `isPublic` is mapped from the API field `public`. `status` is read from `statusExplanation.raw`. Timestamps are ISO-8601 strings parsed into `OffsetDateTime`. ### TypeDto Represents a work package type. Fields: `id`, `name`, `defaultType` (from API field `isDefault`), `milestone` (from API field `isMilestone`), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `href`. ### UserDto Represents the authenticated user extracted from the API root response (`/api/v3`). Fields: `href` and `name` (from `_links.user.href` and `_links.user.title`). Only populated via `UserMapper.fromRoot`. ### RelationDto Represents a relation between work packages. Fields: `id` (always `null` for derived relation types `parent`, `children`, `ancestors`), `type`, `description`, `toId`, `to`. ### RelationValuesDto A Java record (`String[] allowedToValues`) holding the allowed relation type values (`relates`, `blocks`, `precedes`, `duplicates`, `includes`, `requires`). Populated by `RelationTools.relationAllowedValues()` from the `RelationType` enum. ### WorkPackageDto Represents a work package. Fields: `id`, `lockVersion`, `subject`, `description`, `storyPoints`, `startDate`, `dueDate`, `estimatedTime`, `duration`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `type`, `priority`, `href`. The `type` and `priority` name properties are populated from either `_embedded` (single-work-package responses) or `_links` (list responses) depending on context. `description` is read from `description.raw` to obtain the rendered Markdown text. ### WorkPackageCreateDto Input DTO for work package creation. Fields: `subject` (`@NotBlank` in validation group `OnCreate`), `description`, `typeId` (`@NotNull` in group `OnCreate`), `priorityId`, `startDate`, `dueDate`, `estimatedTime`, `storyPoints` (`@Positive`). ### WorkPackageUpdateDto Extends `WorkPackageCreateDto` and adds: `lockVersion` (`@NotNull`), and overrides `subject` and `typeId` to remove the `@NotBlank`/`@NotNull` constraints inherited from the superclass, making these fields optional for partial updates. ### Common DTO conventions All DTOs (except `RelationValuesDto`) are Lombok-powered classes annotated with `@Getter`, `@Setter`, `@With`, `@NoArgsConstructor`, and `@AllArgsConstructor`. They use `@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)` so that null-valued properties are omitted during serialization. Jackson `@JsonProperty` annotations with `@JsonPropertyDescription` Javadoc are applied to each field for API documentation. ## Mappers All mappers are MapStruct `@Mapper` interfaces. Each defines a single `default` method that accepts a `tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode` and returns the corresponding DTO. None of the mappers rely on MapStruct-generated implementations; the `default` methods perform manual field extraction. ### PriorityMapper Maps `id`, `name`, `position` (nullable when the node is missing), and `href` from `_links.self.href`. ### ProjectMapper Maps `id`, `identifier`, `name`, `active`, `isPublic` (from API field `public`), `status` (from `statusExplanation.raw`), `description` (from `description.raw`), `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (parsed via `OffsetDateTime.parse`), and `href`. ### TypeMapper Maps `id`, `name`, `defaultType` (from `isDefault`), `milestone` (from `isMilestone`), `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (parsed), and `href`. ### UserMapper Maps from the API root response (`/api/v3`). Extracts `_links.user.href` → `href` and `_links.user.title` → `name`. Uses `StringUtils.trimToNull` to normalize empty strings. ### RelationMapper Provides three methods: - `fromRelationElement(JsonNode)` — maps a single relation element from `_embedded.relations._embedded.elements[]`, extracting `id`, `type`, `description`, and `toId`/`to` from `_links.to`. - `fromWpLink(String, JsonNode)` — maps a derived relation link (`parent`, `children`, or `ancestors`) from `_links.`, setting `id` to `null`. - `extractWpId(String)` — strips the `WP_PREFIX` (`/api/v3/work_packages/`) from an href string and parses the remainder as an integer. Returns `null` on parse failure. ### WorkPackageMapper Maps `id`, `lockVersion`, `subject`, `description` (from `description.raw`), `storyPoints` (null-safe check), `startDate`/`dueDate` (parsed via `LocalDate.parse`), `estimatedTime`, `duration`, `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (parsed via `OffsetDateTime.parse`), and `href`. The `type` and `priority` name fields use a two-source strategy: first checks `_embedded.type` / `_embedded.priority` for embedded data (single-work-package responses), then falls back to `_links.type.title` / `_links.priority.title` for list responses. ## Null-safety and defensive handling All mappers defensively handle null, missing, or empty JSON nodes: - `node.path("field").asString(null)` returns `null` when the field is missing or not a string. - `node.path("field").isMissingNode()` checks are used before calling `asInt()` on fields that may be absent (e.g., `position` in `PriorityMapper`). - `node.get("field")` with explicit null-checks is used for fields where the absence of the node itself is significant (e.g., `storyPoints` in `WorkPackageMapper`). - Timestamp parsing is guarded: `asString(null)` is checked for non-null before calling `OffsetDateTime.parse` or `LocalDate.parse`. ## Integration with OpenProjectApiClient `OpenProjectApiClient` is a Spring `@Service` that injects all six mappers via constructor. Each public method that fetches data from the OpenProject REST API applies the appropriate mapper to the raw `JsonNode` response: | Client method | Mapper used | |---|---| | `root()` | `UserMapper.fromRoot()` | | `workPackageList()` | `WorkPackageMapper.toDto()` per element | | `workPackageShow()` | `WorkPackageMapper.toDto()` | | `workPackageCreate()` | N/A — sends DTO fields as JSON | | `workPackageUpdate()` | N/A — sends DTO fields as JSON | | `typeList()` | `TypeMapper.toDto()` per element | | `priorityList()` | `PriorityMapper.toDto()` per element | | `projectList()` | `ProjectMapper.toDto()` per element | | `listRelationsForWorkPackage()` | `RelationMapper.fromRelationElement()` + `fromWpLink()` | | `relationAdd()` / `relationDelete()` | N/A | | `relationAddParent()` / `relationDeleteParent()` | N/A | For collection endpoints, `OpenProjectApiClient` delegates element mapping to `RestOperations.mapEmbeddedElements()`, which iterates the `_embedded.elements` array and applies the mapper callback to each element. ## Validation `WorkPackageCreateDto` and `WorkPackageUpdateDto` carry Jakarta Bean Validation annotations. `WorkPackageTools` is annotated with `@Validated`, so Spring automatically validates method arguments before delegation. Tests in `WorkPackageToolsTest` verify that `ConstraintViolationException` is thrown for missing `subject`/`typeId` on create and missing `lockVersion` on update. `RelationTools` is also `@Validated`; `RelationToolsTest` verifies `ConstraintViolationException` is thrown when `relationAdd`, `relationDelete`, `relationAddParent`, `relationList`, or `relationDeleteParent` receive `null` arguments. ## Tests | Test class | Scope | What it verifies | |---|---|---| | `PriorityToolsTest` | Unit (Mockito) | Delegation from `PriorityTools` to `OpenProjectApiClient.priorityList()` | | `ProjectToolsTest` | Unit (Mockito) | Delegation from `ProjectTools` to `OpenProjectApiClient.projectList()` and prompt generation | | `WorkPackageToolsTest` | Integration (`@SpringBootTest`) | Constraint validation on `WorkPackageCreateDto` and `WorkPackageUpdateDto` | | `RelationToolsTest` | Integration (`@SpringBootTest`) | `relationAllowedValues()` returns 6 values; constraint validation on relation tools | | `TypesToolsTest` | Integration (`@SpringBootTest`) | Constraint validation on `typeList` | No dedicated unit tests exist for the mapper interfaces themselves; mapping correctness is exercised indirectly through integration tests that exercise the full client → mapper → DTO pipeline via mocked REST responses.

This page describes how the Spring OpenProject MCP Server is built, deployed, and operated as a Docker container. It covers the Dockerfile layout, multi-platform build process with SBOM attestation, health check probes, and the runtime environment variables that govern its behavior. ## Container Image The Docker image is built from the Eclipse Temurin JRE base image, which provides the Java 25 runtime without a full JDK ([repo://docker/Dockerfile#L1-L3](repo://docker/Dockerfile#L1-L3)). The base image tag is `25.0.4_7-jre-ubi10-minimal` (a minimal UBI 10-based JRE). The image includes the following labels for provenance ([repo://docker/Dockerfile#L5-L7](repo://docker/Dockerfile#L5-L7)): | Label | Value | |-------|-------| | `org.opencontainers.image.licenses` | `MIT` | | `org.opencontainers.image.source` | `https://github.com/tmskln/spring-openproject-mcp-server.git` | | `org.opencontainers.image.description` | `MCP Server for OpenProject API (workpackages)` | ## Build Process ### Multi-Platform Build with SBOM The recommended build command produces a multi-platform image supporting both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` ([repo://README.md#L45-L56](repo://README.md#L45-L56)): ```bash PKG_VERSION="dev" && docker build \ -f docker/Dockerfile \ -t spring-openproject-mcp-server:${PKG_VERSION} \ --attest type=sbom,generator=docker/scout-sbom-indexer:latest \ --label org.opencontainers.image.build-date=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") \ --label org.opencontainers.image.revision=$(git rev-parse HEAD) \ --label org.opencontainers.image.version=${PKG_VERSION} \ --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \ . ``` Key build options: - **`--attest type=sbom`** — generates an SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) attestation using Docker Scout's SBOM indexer. The SBOM is embedded in the image metadata for vulnerability scanning and supply-chain verification. - **`--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64`** — builds a multi-architecture manifest list, enabling deployment on both Intel/AMD64 and ARM64 (e.g., Apple Silicon, AWS Graviton) hosts. - **OCI labels** — `build-date`, `revision`, and `version` labels are injected at build time for traceability. ### SBOM Pre-Conversion Before the Docker build, the Maven build produces a CycloneDX SBOM at `target/classes/META-INF/sbom/application.cdx.json`. This can be converted to SPDX JSON format for optimization using the CycloneDX CLI ([repo://README.md#L37-L43](repo://README.md#L37-L43)): ```bash docker run --rm \ -v "./target/classes/META-INF/sbom:/work" --platform linux/amd64 \ cyclonedx/cyclonedx-cli \ convert \ --input-file /work/application.cdx.json \ --output-file /work/application.spdx.json \ --output-format spdxjson ``` Both the CycloneDX (`.cdx.json`) and SPDX (`.spdx.json`) SBOM files are copied into the Docker image ([repo://docker/Dockerfile#L14-L15](repo://docker/Dockerfile#L14-L15)). ## Dockerfile Layout The Dockerfile ([repo://docker/Dockerfile](repo://docker/Dockerfile)) follows these steps: 1. **Base image** — `eclipse-temurin:25.0.4_7-jre-ubi10-minimal` 2. **WORKDIR** — `/app` 3. **Copy** — the application JAR as `app.jar`, plus `application-prod.properties` and both SBOM files 4. **Create non-root user** — `spring` system user with group ownership of `/app` 5. **Switch user** — `USER spring:spring` (no root privileges at runtime) 6. **EXPOSE** — ports `8080` (HTTP) and `8081` (actuator) 7. **HEALTHCHECK** — queries the readiness probe endpoint 8. **ENTRYPOINT** — starts the JVM with `prod` profile active ### Image Contents | Path in Image | Source | |---------------|--------| | `/app/app.jar` | `target/spring-openproject-mcp-server*.jar` | | `/app/application-prod.properties` | `target/classes/application-prod.properties` | | `/app/application.cdx.json` | `target/classes/META-INF/sbom/application.cdx.json` | | `/app/application.spdx.json` | `target/classes/META-INF/sbom/application.spdx.json` | Note that `application-prod.properties` is placed at the image root (`/app/application-prod.properties`) rather than inside `BOOT-INF/classes`, ensuring it is available even if the Spring Boot classpath layout changes. ## Runtime Configuration ### Profile Activation The `prod` Spring Boot profile is activated via a JVM system property passed at container start ([repo://docker/Dockerfile#L29](repo://docker/Dockerfile#L29)): ``` java -Dspring.profiles.active=prod -jar /app/app.jar ``` The `prod` profile ([repo://src/main/resources/application-prod.properties](repo://src/main/resources/application-prod.properties)) applies the following overrides: - Logging: `ERROR` for Spring framework, `INFO` for the application package - Spring banner disabled - Actuator endpoints exposed only at `/actuator/health` - Kubernetes-style readiness/liveness probes enabled (`management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true`) - Disk space and SSL health checks disabled ### Environment Variables The container accepts two environment variables that control its runtime behavior: #### `OPENPROJECT_URL` (required) The base URL of the OpenProject instance the MCP server connects to. Passed at container launch: ```bash docker run -e OPENPROJECT_URL=https://my-openproject.example.com ... ``` This value is consumed by `HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver` as the default base URL when the `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` header override is not enabled ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L22](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L22)). The default is `https://localhost` ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L22](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L22)). #### `OPENPROJECT_ALLOW_HEADER_BASE_URL` (optional) When set to `true`, the server trusts the `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` HTTP header from incoming MCP requests to override the configured base URL. This enables a single MCP server instance to route requests to multiple OpenProject backends dynamically. ```bash docker run -e OPENPROJECT_ALLOW_HEADER_BASE_URL=true ... ``` When enabled, the MCP client must also supply `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` in its request headers ([repo://README.md#L62-L72](repo://README.md#L62-L72)). The default is `false` ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L23](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L23)). **Security note**: Enabling this feature means any MCP client can redirect API calls to an arbitrary URL. Only enable it in trusted environments. ### No Token Storage The user's OpenProject API token is passed per-request via the `Authorization: Bearer ` header in MCP requests. The token is **never stored in the container** ([repo://README.md#L7](repo://README.md#L7)). It is validated once per request against the OpenProject API and cached for 60 minutes in a Caffeine cache named `auth-validation` ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L6-L8](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L6-L8), [repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidationCache.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidationCache.java)). The cached key is a SHA-256 hash of `baseUrl|token` — the raw token is never stored ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java#L44-L45](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java#L44-L45)). ## Health Check ### Docker HEALTHCHECK The Dockerfile defines a periodic health check ([repo://docker/Dockerfile#L25-L26](repo://docker/Dockerfile#L25-L26)): ```dockerfile HEALTHCHECK --interval=5m --timeout=3s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \ CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8081/actuator/health/readiness | grep -q '"status":"UP"' || exit 1 ``` Parameters: | Parameter | Value | Meaning | |-----------|-------|---------| | `--interval` | 5m | Check every 5 minutes | | `--timeout` | 3s | Fail if the command takes more than 3 seconds | | `--start-period` | 20s | Grace period during container startup; failures during this window don't count toward `--retries` | | `--retries` | 3 | Mark unhealthy after 3 consecutive failures | The command queries the Spring Boot Actuator **readiness** endpoint on the management port (8081) and checks for `"status":"UP"` in the response. ### Actuator Endpoint Configuration The actuator is configured to expose only the health endpoint ([repo://src/main/resources/application-prod.properties](repo://src/main/resources/application-prod.properties)): - Base path: `/actuator` - Exposed endpoints: `health` only - Health details and components hidden (`show-details=never`, `show-components=never`) - Kubernetes probes enabled (enables `/actuator/health/liveness` and `/actuator/health/readiness`) - Disk space and SSL health checks disabled ### Security The actuator endpoint on port 8081 is protected by basic authentication ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L58-L66](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L58-L66)): - URL matcher: `/actuator/**` - `/actuator/health` and `/actuator/health/*` are **permitted without auth** (so the Docker `HEALTHCHECK` can query them) - All other actuator paths require the `ACTUATOR_ADMIN` role - Default credentials: username `admin`, password hash stored in `application.properties` (a placeholder bcrypt hash, not a real password) The MCP endpoints on port 8080 (`/mcp`, `/sse`) use bearer-token authentication via the `McpBearerAuthenticationFilter` ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java)). This filter validates the `Authorization: Bearer ` header against the OpenProject API and is explicitly excluded from global servlet filter registration so it only runs within the Spring Security chain ([repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L46-L55](repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L46-L55)). ## Deployment ### Docker Run The standard deployment command ([repo://README.md#L21-L22](repo://README.md#L21-L22)): ```bash docker run -d \ -p 0.0.0.0:8080:8080 \ -p 0.0.0.0:8081:8081 \ -e OPENPROJECT_URL=https://${yourOpenProjectUrl} \ --tmpfs /tmp \ docker.io/tmskln/spring-openproject-mcp-server:latest ``` The `--tmpfs /tmp` mount ensures temporary files are not persisted across container restarts. ### Published Images The latest image is published at [https://hub.docker.com/r/tmskln/spring-openproject-mcp-server](https://hub.docker.com/r/tmskln/spring-openproject-mcp-server). ## MCP Protocol The MCP server defaults to the **SSE (Server-Sent Events)** protocol ([repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L18](repo://src/main/resources/application.properties#L18)), which exposes: - `GET /sse` — server-to-client streaming endpoint - `POST /mcp/message` — client-to-server message endpoint Alternatively, the **STREAMABLE** protocol (`spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol=STREAMABLE`) exposes a single bidirectional endpoint (`/mcp`) based on the MCP streamable HTTP spec. Only one protocol can be active at a time because the transport defines the wiring, endpoints, and message routing ([repo://README.md#L79-L88](repo://README.md#L79-L88)). ## OpenProject Compatibility The server has been tested against OpenProject versions 14, 15, 16.6, and 17.7 ([repo://README.md#L11](repo://README.md#L11)). The application uses direct JSON value mapping with MapStruct rather than a generated OpenAPI client, which provides better compatibility across OpenProject API version differences ([repo://README.md#L93-L103](repo://README.md#L93-L103)). ## Request Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client as MCP Client participant Server as MCP Server
(:8080) participant Filter as McpBearerAuth Filter participant Validator as TokenValidator participant Cache as Caffeine Cache participant API as OpenProject API participant Actuator as Actuator (:8081) Client->>Server: POST /mcp with Bearer token Server->>Filter: pass through security chain Filter->>Validator: validateCurrentRequestOrThrow() Validator->>Cache: cachedCheckToken(key) alt cache miss Cache-->>Validator: miss Validator->>API: GET /api/v3 (root) API-->>Validator: UserDto Validator->>Cache: store (key, UserDto) 60m else cache hit Cache-->>Validator: ValidatedOpenProjectUser end Validator-->>Filter: ValidatedOpenProjectUser Filter-->>Server: set SecurityContext Server-->>Client: MCP response ``` ## Startup Lifecycle ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> ImagePull: docker pull ImagePull --> ContainerStart: docker run ContainerStart --> JVMInit: java -jar app.jar JVMInit --> ProfileLoad: -Dspring.profiles.active=prod ProfileLoad --> ActuatorReady: health probes enabled ActuatorReady --> MCPActive: SSE/STREAMABLE transport MCPActive --> Running: ready Running --> HealthCheck: HEALTHCHECK every 5m HealthCheck --> Running: status=UP HealthCheck --> Unhealthy: 3 consecutive failures ``` ## Integration Testing Integration tests run against a real OpenProject container ([repo://README.md#L74-L76](repo://README.md#L74-L76)): ```bash mvn test -Dopenproject.container.tag=17.5.1 -Dopenproject.container.port=18080 ``` Tests use the `STREAMABLE` protocol to avoid leaving open SSE streams during teardown ([repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpPingIntegrationTest.java#L22](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpPingIntegrationTest.java#L22)). Volumes should be removed between test runs to avoid state leakage.

nodes.title: Quickstart
nodes.body:
## Spring OpenProject MCP Server

This project implements an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server in Java that proxies OpenProject's REST API, enabling AI agents to manage work packages, projects, priorities, types, and relations through standardized tool and prompt calls. The server authenticates each request via a user-provided OpenProject bearer token (never stored in the container), resolves the target OpenProject URL, and delegates REST calls through a `RestClient`-based client with HAL+JSON parsing and Freemarker payload rendering.

**Key facts**

- **Stack**: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Spring AI MCP Server 2.0.1 · Java 25 · Tomcat 11.0.26
- **Ports**: `8080` (MCP / app) · `8081` (Actuator health)
- **Protocol**: SSE (default) or STREAMABLE via `spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol`
- **Profiles**: `dev`, `local`, `prod`, `test`
- **Compatibility**: OpenProject 14, 15, 16.6, 17.7
- **Auth**: Bearer token in `Authorization` header; optional multi-tenant URL via `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` header
- **Env vars**: `OPENPROJECT_URL`, `OPENPROJECT_ALLOW_HEADER_BASE_URL`

## Wiki Routing Map

### Architecture

| Page | What it covers |
|------|----------------|
| [System Overview](architecture/overview.md) | High-level component diagram and boundaries |
| [MCP Protocol Layer](architecture/mcp-protocol.md) | Tool/prompt registration, SSE vs STREAMABLE transport |
| [OpenProject REST Client](architecture/openproject-client.md) | `OpenProjectApiClient`, connection resolver, HAL+JSON parsing, Freemarker templates |
| [Security Architecture](architecture/security.md) | Bearer validation, Spring Security filter chains, Caffeine token cache |

### Concepts

| Page | What it covers |
|------|----------------|
| [Configuration and Profiles](concepts/configuration.md) | `application-{profile}.properties`, profile selection, MCP protocol config |
| [DTOs and Mappers](concepts/dtos-and-mappers.md) | WorkPackage, Project, Priority, Type, Relation, User DTOs and MapStruct mappers |

### Workflows

| Page | What it covers |
|------|----------------|
| [MCP Request Flow](workflows/mcp-request-flow.md) | End-to-end: initialize → auth → tool dispatch → OpenProject API → response |
| [Work Package Lifecycle](workflows/work-package-lifecycle.md) | Create, update, safe-edit prompt, lockVersion optimistic locking, attachment upload |

### Operations

| Page | What it covers |
|------|----------------|
| [Deployment](operations/deployment.md) | Docker image, multi-platform build, SBOM, health check, env vars |

### Testing

| Page | What it covers |
|------|----------------|
| [Integration Testing](testing/integration-tests.md) | `SpringBootTest` with `RANDOM_PORT`, MCP test helpers, Docker Compose OpenProject, unit tests |

## Getting Started Locally

1. Set `OPENPROJECT_URL` to your OpenProject instance.
2. Start the container:

   ```bash
   docker run -d -p 0.0.0.0:8080:8080 \
     -e OPENPROJECT_URL=https://your-openproject-url \
     --tmpfs /tmp \
     docker.io/tmskln/spring-openproject-mcp-server:latest
   ```

3. Configure your MCP client (e.g. LM Studio) with the SSE endpoint and your OpenProject API token:

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "openproject-mcp": {
         "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/sse",
         "headers": {
           "Authorization": "Bearer {yourToken}"
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

4. Prompt the MCP tools, e.g. `"List all projects in OpenProject using mcp/openproject-mcp."`

For multi-tenant setups, enable header-based URL resolution:

```bash
-e OPENPROJECT_ALLOW_HEADER_BASE_URL=true
```

Then include `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` in each MCP client request header.

nodes.body:
## Overview

The project uses two tiers of testing: **unit tests** for utility classes (e.g., `PatchMap`) and **integration tests** for the MCP protocol layer and the `OpenProjectApiClient` against a real OpenProject instance. Integration tests are driven by Spring Boot's `@SpringBootTest` with `RANDOM_PORT` for local MCP endpoint tests and by an externally managed Docker Compose container for remote API tests. Test discovery is controlled by JUnit 5 tags (`integration_local`, `integration_remote`, `security`).

## Test Tagging and Discovery

Test constants are centralized in [TestConstants](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/TestConstants.java):

- `TAG_INTEGRATION_TEST_LOCAL` (`"integration_local"`) — local MCP protocol tests that start an embedded server.
- `TAG_INTEGRATION_TEST_REMOTE` (`"integration_remote"`) — tests that require a real OpenProject instance.
- `TAG_SECURITY` (`"security"`) — marks security-specific parameterized tests.

These tags are applied via `@Tag(...)` on test classes and individual methods, enabling selective test execution via Maven Surefire/Failsafe filters or IDE run configurations.

## Local MCP Protocol Tests

Tests in the `tools` package exercise the MCP server over HTTP against an embedded Spring Boot application. All use `SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT` to avoid port conflicts.

### Test Helper: `McpToolsHelper`

[McpToolsHelper](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsHelper.java) is a static utility that encapsulates the raw MCP protocol interaction:

- **`initializeAndGetSessionId(port)`** — Sends an MCP `initialize` JSON-RPC request to `/mcp`, asserts a 200 response, extracts the `Mcp-Session-Id` header, and returns the session ID for subsequent calls.
- **`initializeMcp(port, extraHeaders)`** — Builds and sends the raw `initialize` request with protocol version `2024-11-05`, `Accept: text/event-stream, application/json`, and the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header.
- **`callToolsList(port, sessionId)` / `callPromptsList(port, sessionId)`** — Sends `tools/list` and `prompts/list` JSON-RPC requests to `/mcp` with the session ID, parses the SSE-wrapped JSON-RPC response via `parseJsonRpcFromSse()`.
- **`callPing(port, sessionId)`** — Sends a `ping` JSON-RPC request and returns the parsed `JsonNode`.
- **`callToolsListRequest(port, sessionId, extraHeaders, expectStatus)`** — Overload that accepts an expected status code; when the expected status is not 200, it discards the response body and returns `null` after asserting the status.
- A shared `HttpClient` instance with a 5-second connect timeout is reused across all calls.

The helper parses SSE-delimited JSON-RPC responses by stripping the SSE framing, enabling assertions on the raw JSON-RPC structure (e.g., `jsonrpc` field, `id`, `error` absence).

### `McpPingIntegrationTest`

Verifies the MCP `ping` method returns valid JSON-RPC 2.0:

- Asserts `jsonrpc == "2.0"`, presence of `id`, and absence of `error`.
- Asserts `result` is a JSON object (empty result for ping).
- Uses `STREAMABLE` protocol via `spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol=STREAMABLE` to avoid keeping an SSE stream open during the test.
- Imports `McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig` to bypass authentication for this basic protocol test.

### `McpToolsListIntegrationTest`

Verifies the MCP `tools/list` method:

- Asserts JSON-RPC 2.0 compliance (jsonrpc, id, no error).
- Asserts all 14 expected tools are present by name: `priorityList`, `projectList`, `relationAdd`, `relationAddParent`, `relationAllowedValues`, `relationDelete`, `relationDeleteParent`, `relationList`, `typeList`, `workPackageCreate`, `workPackageList`, `workPackageShow`, `workPackageUpdate`, `workPackageUploadAttachment`.
- Asserts every tool has a non-blank `name`, `description`, and an `inputSchema` of type `object` or empty.
- Uses JsonPath (`com.jayway.jsonpath:json-path`) to assert tool names can be extracted from the raw JSON response and that no names are blank.
- Concrete schema validation for `relationAdd`: checks `required` fields (`workPackageId`, `otherWorkPackageId`, `relationType`) and field-level descriptions in `inputSchema.properties`.

### `McpPromptsIntegrationTest`

Verifies the MCP `prompts/list` method:

- Asserts JSON-RPC 2.0 compliance.
- Asserts the response contains the expected prompts from the application: `openproject.workpackage.safe_edit` and `openproject.project.summary`.
- Asserts every prompt has a non-blank `name` and `description`.
- Parameterized test verifies specific prompt name/description pairs.

### `McpSecurityIntegrationTest`

Tests MCP authentication at the protocol level using parameterized tests (`@CsvSource`). This test class **does not** import `McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig`, so real Spring Security applies.

**Authentication stub**: The inner `McpHeaderAwareTokenValidatorTestConfig` class provides a `@Primary` `OpenProjectTokenValidator` bean that overrides `fetchUserFromOpenProject()`:

- If the bearer token equals `"correctToken"`, it returns a fake `UserDto`.
- Otherwise, it throws `UnauthorizedException`.

**Tested scenarios** (parameterized with `correctToken→200`, `wrongToken→401`, `empty→401`, `null→401`):

- **`mcpInitializeAuth`** — The `initialize` request must include a valid `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header; without it or with a wrong token, the server returns 401.
- **`mcpToolsRequestWithoutInitializeAuth`** — `tools/list` sent with a `fakeSessionId` (never initialized) returns 401 regardless of the token.
- **`mcpToolsRequestWithCorrectMCPSession`** — After a valid `initialize`, subsequent `tools/list` requests accept both the correct token and any token (because the session was already validated during initialize).
- **`mcpPingRequestWithoutInitializeAuth` / `mcpPingRequestWithCorrectMcpSession`** — Same pattern for the `ping` method.
- **`mcpPromptsRequestWithCorrectMcpSession` / `mcpPromptsRequestWithoutInitializeAuth`** — Same pattern for the `prompts/list` method.

These tests confirm that: (1) authentication is enforced on `initialize`, (2) the session binding is correct, and (3) unauthorized requests to any MCP method are rejected with 401.

## Security Stub Configuration

[McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig.java) is a `@TestConfiguration` that overrides the production `SecurityFilterChain` for MCP endpoints:

```java
@Bean @Order(0)
SecurityFilterChain testMcpPermitAll(HttpSecurity http) {
    http
        .securityMatcher("/mcp", "/mcp/**", "/sse")
        .authorizeHttpRequests(reg -> reg.anyRequest().permitAll())
        .csrf(AbstractHttpConfigurer::disable)
        .httpBasic(AbstractHttpConfigurer::disable);
    return http.build();
}
```

- **Order 0** ensures it takes priority over the production MCP filter chain (order 2).
- It matches `/mcp`, `/mcp/**`, and `/sse` endpoints and permits all requests.
- CSRF and HTTP Basic are disabled to avoid interference.
- Imported via `@Import(McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig.class)` on `McpPingIntegrationTest`, `McpToolsListIntegrationTest`, and `McpPromptsIntegrationTest`.

## Remote Integration Test: `OpenProjectApiClient`

[OpenProjectApiClientIntegrationTest](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClientIntegrationTest.java) is the heavyweight integration test that spins up a real OpenProject Docker container and exercises the full `OpenProjectApiClient` against it.

### Container Lifecycle

The test manages the OpenProject container lifecycle through an `ApplicationContextInitializer`:

1. **`OpenProjectInitializer.initialize()`** — Reads `openproject.container.tag`, `openproject.container.port`, and `openproject.container.shutdown` from the Spring environment. Calls `ensureStarted()` which:
   - Runs `docker compose -f src/test/resources/openproject/docker-compose.yml up -d --pull always` with environment variables for image tag, port, and hostname.
   - Polls the container's health endpoint (`/api/v3`) with a 5-minute timeout, retrying every 3 seconds.
   - Generates an admin API key by executing a Rails runner script inside the container (`bundle exec rails runner`) that finds the admin user and extracts the plain API token.
   - Applies `openproject.url=<baseUrl>` as a test property via `TestPropertyValues`.

2. **`afterAll()`** — If `openproject.container.shutdown=true` (the default), runs `docker compose down -v` to tear down the container and volumes.

3. **`ensureStarted()`** is `synchronized` to prevent concurrent test threads from starting multiple containers.

### TestAuthConfig Stub

A `@TestConfiguration` inner class (`TestAuthConfig`) provides a `@Primary` `OpenProjectConnectionResolver` bean that returns a hardcoded `OpenProjectConnection` with the container's base URL and generated API key. This bypasses the production connection resolver so the `OpenProjectApiClient` always talks to the test container regardless of application properties.

### Test Setup (`initIds`)

After the container is ready:

1. Calls `client.root()` to verify the API key works and the connection is valid.
2. Finds the `"Demo project"` from `client.projectList()` (seeded via `OPENPROJECT_SEED_DUMMY_DATA=true`).
3. Caches `demoProjectId`, `demoTypeId`, and `demoPriorityId` for use in individual tests.

### Test Cases

| Test | What It Verifies |
|------|-----------------|
| `root_returnsAuthenticatedUser` | `client.root()` returns a non-null `UserDto` with a non-blank `href`. |
| `projectList_containsDemoProject` | `client.projectList()` includes a project named `"Demo project"`. |
| `workPackageShow_withNonExistentWpId` | `client.workPackageShow(Integer.MAX_VALUE)` returns `null` (404 → null contract). |
| `relationDelete_withNonExistentRelationId_returnsFalse` | `client.relationDelete(Integer.MAX_VALUE)` returns `false` (not an exception). |
| `relationAdd_withNonExistentWorkPackageId_returnsFalse` | Adding a relation with a non-existent work package ID throws `HttpClientErrorException` with status 422. |
| `workPackageList_withNonExistentProjectId_throws404Exception` | Listing work packages for a non-existent project throws `RestClientResponseException` with status 404. |
| `priorityList_returnsNonEmptyList_withIdsAndNames` | `client.priorityList()` returns non-empty entries with valid IDs and names. |
| `typeList_forDemoProject_returnsNonEmptyList_withIdsAndNames` | `client.typeList(demoProjectId)` returns valid type entries. |
| `workPackageCrud_and_attachments_and_relations_areFunctional` | Full end-to-end CRUD: create two work packages, list, show, update subject (with lockVersion), upload attachment, add relation, list relations, delete relation, add/delete parent relation, verify all succeed. |

### Docker Compose Configuration

[src/test/resources/openproject/docker-compose.yml](repo://src/test/resources/openproject/docker-compose.yml) defines the test OpenProject service:

- **Image**: `openproject/openproject:${OPENPROJECT_IMAGE_TAG}` (tag overridden by `application-test.properties`, default `17.7.2`).
- **Port mapping**: `${OPENPROJECT_PORT:-8088}:80`.
- **Environment**: `OPENPROJECT_HOST__NAME`, `OPENPROJECT_HTTPS=false`, `OPENPROJECT_SEED_DUMMY_DATA=true`, `OPENPROJECT_EMAIL__DELIVERY__METHOD=smtp`, `OPENPROJECT_DISABLE__SECRET_KEY_BASE__CHECK=true`.
- **Health check**: `wget -qO- http://localhost/api/v3` with 10s interval, 5s timeout, 60 retries.

### Test Properties

[src/test/resources/application-test.properties](repo://src/test/resources/application-test.properties) provides:

- `openproject.container.tag=17.7.2` — Docker image tag.
- `openproject.container.shutdown=false` — Whether to tear down the container after tests.
- `openproject.container.port=18088` — Host port for the container.
- `openproject.allow-header-base-url=false` — Disables header-based URL override in production.

## Unit Test: `PatchMap`

[PatchMapTest](repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/util/PatchMapTest.java) exercises the `PatchMap` utility class (used by `OpenProjectApiClient` for building JSON patch bodies):

- **`of(Nullable.DROP_NULL_VALUES, ...)`** — Filters out entries with `null` values; empty strings, `0`, and `false` are preserved.
- **`of(Nullable.ALLOW_NULL_VALUES, ...)`** — Includes `null` values in the result map.
- **`of(Nullable.DROP_NULL_VALUES)`** with no pairs — Returns an empty map.
- **Odd argument count** — Throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `"Number of  arguments must be even"`.
- **Non-string key** — Throws `ClassCastException`.
- **Mixed types** — Correctly handles `String`, `Integer`, and `Boolean` values.

## Test Architecture Summary

```
src/test/
├── java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/
│   ├── TestConstants.java              # Shared tag constants
│   ├── tools/
│   │   ├── McpToolsHelper.java         # MCP protocol test utilities
│   │   ├── McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig.java  # Permit-all security stub
│   │   ├── McpPingIntegrationTest.java     # ping method test
│   │   ├── McpPromptsIntegrationTest.java  # prompts/list test
│   │   ├── McpSecurityIntegrationTest.java # Auth/authorization tests
│   │   └── McpToolsListIntegrationTest.java# tools/list test
│   └── openproject/client/
│       └── OpenProjectApiClientIntegrationTest.java  # Docker + API tests
└── resources/
    ├── application-test.properties     # Container config overrides
    └── openproject/
        └── docker-compose.yml          # OpenProject container definition
```

All local MCP integration tests share a common pattern:

1. `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` to start an embedded server.
2. `@Import(McpNoAuthTestSecurityConfig.class)` to disable auth (except `McpSecurityIntegrationTest`).
3. `@Tag(TestConstants.TAG_INTEGRATION_TEST_LOCAL)` for selective execution.
4. `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` for `@BeforeAll`/`@AfterAll` shared state.
5. `@LocalServerPort` to obtain the random port at runtime.
6. `McpToolsHelper` to perform raw HTTP interactions against the embedded server.

The remote `OpenProjectApiClientIntegrationTest` differs in that it uses `@Tag(TestConstants.TAG_INTEGRATION_TEST_REMOTE)`, does not use `RANDOM_PORT` (the server runs inside the container), and manages its own Docker Compose lifecycle via `ApplicationContextInitializer`.

nodes.body:
# MCP Request Flow

This page traces the complete lifecycle of an MCP (Model Context Protocol) request in the OpenProject MCP server, from client initialization through authentication, tool/prompt dispatch, OpenProject API interaction, and response delivery.

## Protocol Overview

The server supports two MCP transport protocols, both served over HTTP at `/mcp`:

- **SSE (Server-Sent Events)**: The client first connects to `/sse` to receive an SSE stream, which includes a `Mcp-Session-Id` header. Subsequent JSON-RPC requests are POSTed to `/mcp` with that session ID in the `Mcp-Session-Id` header.
- **STREAMABLE**: All communication happens via HTTP POST to `/mcp` with session tracking handled through response headers (`Mcp-Session-Id`).

Both protocols use JSON-RPC 2.0 as the message format. The protocol version used is `2024-11-05` [[repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsHelper.java#L22-L23]].

The server is configured for STREAMABLE mode by default in tests via `spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol=STREAMABLE` [[repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpSecurityIntegrationTest.java#L39]].

## Authentication Flow

### Entry Point: Security Filter Chain

Spring Security configures two filter chains in `SecurityConfig` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L34-L84]]:

1. **Actuator chain** (`@Order(1)`): Matches `/actuator/**`. Requires HTTP Basic auth with `ACTUATOR_ADMIN` role for all endpoints except `/actuator/health` and `/actuator/health/*` which are permitted without auth [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L57-L63]].

2. **MCP chain** (`@Order(2)`): Matches `/mcp/**`, `/mcp`, `/error`, and `/sse`. Requires all requests to be authenticated via Bearer token. HTTP Basic is explicitly disabled for this chain [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L72-L82]].

The `McpBearerAuthenticationFilter` is injected into the MCP chain via `addFilterBefore(..., UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter.class)` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L75]].

### Filter Registration

`McpBearerAuthenticationFilter` is a `@Component`, but Spring Boot's auto-registration is explicitly disabled by a `FilterRegistrationBean` with `setEnabled(false)` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/SecurityConfig.java#L46-L55]]. This ensures the filter only operates within the Spring Security chain, not as a global servlet filter.

### Bearer Token Validation

`McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.doFilterInternal()` processes every incoming request to `/mcp`, `/sse`, or their sub-paths [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java#L45-L47]]:

1. **Filter exclusion**: `shouldNotFilter()` skips requests whose URI does not match `/sse`, `/mcp`, or paths starting with `/mcp/` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java#L32-L35]].

2. **Async dispatch**: `shouldNotFilterAsyncDispatch()` returns `false` to ensure authentication runs on async dispatches (critical for SSE) [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java#L39-L41]].

3. **Token validation**: Calls `OpenProjectTokenValidator.validateCurrentRequestOrThrow()`:
   - `OpenProjectConnectionResolver` (default: `HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver`) extracts the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and the `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` header (if `openproject.allow-header-base-url` is true) from the current request [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java#L30-L48]].
   - The token is SHA-256 hashed (combined with the base URL) to produce a cache key. The raw token is never stored in the cache [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java#L41-L42]].
   - `OpenProjectTokenValidationCache.cachedCheckToken()` performs a Spring Cache lookup with `cacheNames = "auth-validation"` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidationCache.java#L16-L17]]. On cache miss, it calls `fetchUserFromOpenProject()` which invokes `OpenProjectApiClient.root()` to call `GET /api/v3` on OpenProject. A successful response (non-null `href`) proves the token is valid [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java#L51-L60]].

4. **Security context**: On success, a `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` with `ROLE_MCP_USER` authority is created and stored in `SecurityContextHolder`, then persisted via `RequestAttributeSecurityContextRepository` for async dispatch recovery [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java#L54-L60]].

5. **Failure**: On `UnauthorizedException`, the security context is cleared and a `401 Unauthorized` response with body `{"error":"unauthorized"}` is written [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java#L62-L66]].

### Test Stubbing

Tests use `McpSecurityIntegrationTest.McpHeaderAwareTokenValidatorTestConfig` which provides a `@Primary` `OpenProjectTokenValidator` bean that stubs `fetchUserFromOpenProject()` to accept only `VALID_TOKEN = "correctToken"` and reject all others [[repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpSecurityIntegrationTest.java#L62-L77]].

## Request Dispatch

### Initialization

The MCP client sends an `initialize` JSON-RPC request to `/mcp` containing:
- `protocolVersion`: `"2024-11-05"`
- `capabilities`: client capabilities
- `clientInfo`: name and version

On success, the server returns the initialization response and, in SSE mode, the `Mcp-Session-Id` header for subsequent requests [[repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsHelper.java#L58-L79]].

### Tool Dispatch

Tool methods are defined via `@McpTool` annotations on Spring `@Component` beans in the `tools` package:

| Tool Class | MCP Tools |
|---|---|
| `WorkPackageTools` | `workPackageList`, `workPackageShow`, `workPackageCreate`, `workPackageUpdate`, `workPackageUploadAttachment` |
| `PriorityTools` | `priorityList` |
| `ProjectTools` | `projectList` |
| `RelationTools` | `relationAllowedValues`, `relationList`, `relationAdd`, `relationDelete`, `relationAddParent`, `relationDeleteParent` |
| `TypesTools` | `typeList` |

Each tool method delegates to `OpenProjectApiClient` for the actual API call. The `@McpTool` annotation provides the tool name (derived from the method name), description, and `readOnlyHint` metadata for the MCP protocol [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/WorkPackageTools.java#L44-L104]][[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/RelationTools.java#L34-L76]].

### Prompt Dispatch

Prompts are defined via `@McpPrompt` annotations:

| Prompt | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `openproject.workpackage.safe_edit` | Safe edit workflow with diff + confirmation, lockVersion handling, Markdown `/n` newline directive [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/WorkPackageTools.java#L106-L142]] |
| `openproject.project.summary` | Project summary generation [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/ProjectTools.java#L38-L47]] |

### Logging

`Common` class provides an `@McpLogging` handler that receives MCP logging notifications and logs them via SLF4J [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/Common.java#L15-L19]].

## OpenProject API Interaction

### Client Factory

`OpenProjectRestClientFactory` creates a `RestClient` per request:
1. Resolves `OpenProjectConnection` (base URL + bearer token) via `OpenProjectConnectionResolver`
2. Converts the bearer token to an OpenProject-compatible `Authorization: Basic <base64(apikey:token)>` header via `OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory.java#L12-L17]]
3. Clones the Spring `RestClient.Builder` and sets the base URL and default header [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestClientFactory.java#L17-L23]]

### REST Operations

`OpenProjectRestOperations` wraps HTTP operations with HAL+JSON content negotiation:

- **GET**: `getJson(uriTemplate, ...)` — `Accept: application/hal+json` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L33-L38]]
- **POST**: `postJson(uriTemplate, jsonBody, ...)` — `Content-Type: application/json`, `Accept: application/hal+json` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L40-L46]]
- **PATCH**: `patchJson(uriTemplate, jsonBody, ...)` — same headers as POST [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L48-L54]]
- **DELETE**: `delete(uriTemplate, ...)` — `Accept: application/hal+json`, returns bodiless entity [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L56-L60]]
- **Multipart POST**: `postMultipart(uriTemplate, body, ...)` — `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` for attachment uploads [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L62-L68]]

JSON bodies are constructed via FreeMarker templates (`OpenProjectTemplateRenderer`) that render PatchMap models (e.g., `create_work_package.ftl`, `update_parent_relation.ftl`) [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L71-L90]][[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectTemplateRenderer.java#L19-L26]].

### Work Package Lifecycle Operations

`OpenProjectApiClient` provides the core OpenProject API methods:

- **`workPackageList(projectId)`**: GET `/api/v3/projects/{projectId}/work_packages?pageSize=1000`, maps `_embedded.elements` via `WorkPackageMapper` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L57-L61]]
- **`workPackageShow(wpId)`**: GET `/api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}`, returns `null` on 404 [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L63-L70]]
- **`workPackageCreate(projectId, dto)`**: POST `/api/v3/projects/{projectId}/work_packages` with FreeMarker-rendered JSON, returns new work package ID [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L72-L84]]
- **`workPackageUpdate(wpId, dto)`**: PATCH `/api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}` with lockVersion, returns `true` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L86-L99]]
- **`workPackageUploadAttachment(wpId, fileName, content, contentType)`**: POST multipart with metadata + file parts [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L101-L106]]

### Relation Resolution

`listRelationsForWorkPackage()` assembles relations from four sources:
1. `_embedded.relations._embedded.elements` (explicit relations)
2. `_links.parent` (derived parent relation)
3. `_links.children[]` (derived children)
4. `_links.ancestors[]` (derived ancestors)

This multi-source approach is necessary because OpenProject exposes parent/child/ancestor relationships through `_links` rather than the `_embedded.relations` structure [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L120-L167]].

## Response Delivery

### STREAMABLE Protocol

The server responds with JSON-RPC responses over HTTP. Session state is managed via the `Mcp-Session-Id` response header. Each request is authenticated independently via the `Authorization` header.

### SSE Protocol

The server streams Server-Sent Events to the client. JSON-RPC responses are delivered as SSE `data:` events. The `Mcp-Session-Id` header in the initial SSE connection is used for subsequent request correlation.

### Error Handling

- **Authentication failure**: `401 Unauthorized` with `{"error":"unauthorized"}` [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/McpBearerAuthenticationFilter.java#L62-L66]]
- **Missing OpenProject URL/token**: `UnauthorizedException` with descriptive message [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java#L35-L40]]
- **Invalid OpenProject token**: `UnauthorizedException` with HTTP status from OpenProject's response [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java#L58-L60]]
- **404 on work package show**: Returns `null` rather than propagating the exception [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L66-L68]]
- **Relation delete failure**: Logs warning and returns `false` rather than throwing [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L179-L185]]

## Connection Resolver Switching

`OpenProjectConnectionResolver` is an interface with two implementations:

1. **`HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver`** (active `@Component`): Extracts `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` and `Authorization` headers from the current `HttpServletRequest`. Falls back to `openproject.url` config for the base URL. The `X-OpenProject-Base-Url` header usage is controlled by `openproject.allow-header-base-url` (default: `false`) [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/HttpHeaderOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java#L22-L54]].

2. **`EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver`** (commented out `@Component`): Reads `OPENPROJECT_BASE_URL` and `OPENPROJECT_BEARER_TOKEN` from environment variables. Provided as a future alternative for STDIO transport where HTTP headers are not available [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/EnvOpenProjectConnectionResolver.java#L10-L18]].

## Tests

Integration tests in the `tools` package verify the complete request flow:

- **`McpSecurityIntegrationTest`**: Parameterized tests covering initialization auth, tools/list auth, prompts/list auth, and ping auth — each with valid token, wrong token, and missing token scenarios [[repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpSecurityIntegrationTest.java#L43-L136]].

- **`McpToolsHelper`**: Test utility that constructs raw HTTP requests with the correct MCP headers (`MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Session-Id`, `Accept: text/event-stream, application/json`), sends them to a random-port server, and parses SSE or JSON responses [[repo://src/test/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/tools/McpToolsHelper.java#L33-L310]].

- **`McpPingIntegrationTest`**, **`McpPromptsIntegrationTest`**, **`McpToolsListIntegrationTest`**: Protocol-level tests for ping, prompts, and tools endpoints respectively.

- **`WorkPackageToolsTest`**, **`RelationToolsTest`**, etc.: Unit tests for individual tool classes.

## Mermaid Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as MCP Client
    participant Server as MCP Server
    participant Filter as McpBearerAuthFilter
    participant Validator as OpenProjectTokenValidator
    participant Cache as TokenValidationCache
    participant OP as OpenProject API

    Client->>Server: POST /mcp (initialize)
    Server->>Filter: doFilterInternal()
    Filter->>Validator: validateCurrentRequestOrThrow()
    Validator->>Validator: resolve OpenProjectConnection
    Validator->>Validator: SHA-256 hash(token + baseUrl)
    Validator->>Cache: cachedCheckToken(key, supplier)
    alt Cache hit
        Cache-->>Validator: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    else Cache miss
        Validator->>OP: GET /api/v3 (Authorization: Basic <apikey:token>)
        OP-->>Validator: UserDto (href, name)
        Validator->>Cache: store(key, user)
        Cache-->>Validator: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    end
    Validator-->>Filter: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    Filter->>Filter: Set SecurityContext (ROLE_MCP_USER)
    Filter-->>Server: continue chain
    Server-->>Client: JSON-RPC response + Mcp-Session-Id

    Client->>Server: POST /mcp (tools/list)
    Server->>Filter: doFilterInternal()
    Filter->>Validator: validateCurrentRequestOrThrow()
    Validator->>Cache: cachedCheckToken(key)
    Cache-->>Validator: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    Validator-->>Filter: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    Filter-->>Server: continue chain
    Server->>Server: dispatch to WorkPackageTools / ProjectTools / etc.
    Server->>OP: GET /api/v3/projects/{id}/work_packages
    OP-->>Server: HAL+JSON WorkPackage[]
    Server-->>Client: JSON-RPC response

    Client->>Server: POST /mcp (tools/call)
    Server->>Filter: doFilterInternal()
    Filter->>Validator: validateCurrentRequestOrThrow()
    Validator->>Cache: cachedCheckToken(key)
    Cache-->>Validator: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    Validator-->>Filter: ValidatedOpenProjectUser
    Filter-->>Server: continue chain
    Server->>Server: dispatch to specific tool method
    Server->>OP: POST/PATCH /api/v3/work_packages/{id}
    OP-->>Server: HAL+JSON response
    Server-->>Client: JSON-RPC response
```

## Key Invariants

1. **Token caching**: Every validated token is cached by its SHA-256 hash. The raw token is never stored in the cache, preventing token leakage in cache stores [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidator.java#L41-L42]][[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/security/OpenProjectTokenValidationCache.java#L16-L17]].

2. **Bearer-to-Basic conversion**: The MCP-level `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header is converted to `Authorization: Basic <base64(apikey:<token>)>` for OpenProject API calls [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectAuthHeaderFactory.java#L12-L17]].

3. **Per-request RestClient**: Each OpenProject API call gets a fresh `RestClient` instance with the current connection's base URL and auth header, preventing stale configuration [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestClientFactory.java#L17-L23]].

4. **HAL+JSON content negotiation**: All OpenProject API calls use `Accept: application/hal+json` and parse `_embedded.elements` arrays for collection responses [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L33-L38]][[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectRestOperations.java#L93-L101]].

5. **PatchMap models**: OpenProject API JSON bodies are constructed via FreeMarker templates from `PatchMap` models, enabling selective field updates (PATCH semantics) rather than full object serialization [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L71-L90]].

6. **Multi-source relation resolution**: Work package relations are assembled from both `_embedded.relations` and `_links` (parent, children, ancestors), requiring a combined approach not all MCP clients may anticipate [[repo://src/main/java/de/tklein/tklab/openproject/mcp/openproject/client/OpenProjectApiClient.java#L120-L167]].

# Work Package Lifecycle

This page traces how the OpenProject MCP server creates, updates, and manages
work packages through its tool layer, covering validation, payload rendering,
optimistic locking, attachment upload, and parent/child relation handling.

## Architecture Overview

Work package operations flow through three layers:

1. **MCP Tool layer** (`WorkPackageTools`, `RelationTools`) — receives tool
   calls from MCP clients, applies Bean Validation, delegates to the API client.
2. **API client** (`OpenProjectApiClient`) — builds data models via `PatchMap`,
   renders Freemarker templates into JSON payloads, and dispatches HTTP requests
   to the OpenProject REST API.
3. **OpenProject REST API** — persists work packages, enforces server-side
   constraints, and returns JSON responses.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as MCP Client
    participant Tools as WorkPackageTools / RelationTools
    participant ClientSvc as OpenProjectApiClient
    participant Template as Freemarker
    participant API as OpenProject REST API

    Client->>Tools: workPackageCreate(projectId, WorkPackageCreateDto)
    Tools->>Tools: Bean Validation (OnCreate + Default)
    Tools->>ClientSvc: workPackageCreate(projectId, dto)
    ClientSvc->>ClientSvc: PatchMap.of(ALLOW_NULL_VALUES, ...)
    ClientSvc->>Template: render("create_work_package.ftl", model)
    Template-->>ClientSvc: JSON payload
    ClientSvc->>API: POST /api/v3/projects/{projectId}/work_packages
    API-->>ClientSvc: {id}
    ClientSvc-->>Tools: Integer workPackageId
    Tools-->>Client: Integer workPackageId

    Client->>Tools: workPackageUpdate(workPackageId, WorkPackageUpdateDto)
    Tools->>Tools: Bean Validation (lockVersion required)
    Tools->>ClientSvc: workPackageUpdate(wpId, dto)
    ClientSvc->>ClientSvc: PatchMap.of(ALLOW_NULL_VALUES, ...)
    ClientSvc->>Template: render("update_work_package.ftl", model)
    Template-->>ClientSvc: JSON payload
    ClientSvc->>API: PATCH /api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}
    API-->>ClientSvc: (success / lockVersion conflict)
    ClientSvc-->>Tools: boolean
    Tools-->>Client: boolean
```

## DTOs and Validation

### WorkPackageCreateDto

Used as the input contract for creation. Validated with `@Validated({OnCreate.class, Default.class})` on the tool method, which activates two constraint groups:

- **OnCreate group**: `subject` is `@NotBlank`, `typeId` is `@NotNull`.
- **Default group**: `storyPoints` is `@Positive` (if present).

All other fields (`description`, `priorityId`, `startDate`, `dueDate`, `estimatedTime`) are optional.

### WorkPackageUpdateDto

Extends `WorkPackageCreateDto` and adds one required field:

- **lockVersion**: `@NotNull` — the latest lock version from the server-side
  work package state. This field is **not** inherited from the superclass; it
  is declared explicitly on the subclass to avoid validation ambiguity.

The `subject` and `typeId` fields are overridden on the subclass with plain
`@JsonProperty` (no `required = true`), making them optional for updates — only
the fields actually present in the request payload are sent to the server.

### WorkPackageDto

The read-side DTO returned from the API. Contains `id`, `lockVersion`,
`subject`, `description`, `storyPoints`, `startDate`, `dueDate`, `estimatedTime`,
`duration`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `type`, `priority`, and `href`.

### RelationDto

Represents a relation reference (including derived `parent`, `children`,
`ancestors` types). Fields: `id` (null for derived relations), `type`,
`description`, `toId`, `to` (title).

## Create Flow

The `workPackageCreate` MCP tool accepts a `projectId` and a `WorkPackageCreateDto`, applies Bean Validation, then delegates to `OpenProjectApiClient.workPackageCreate()`.

1. **Model building**: `PatchMap.of(ALLOW_NULL_VALUES, ...)` creates a map of
   template variables from the DTO fields, preserving `null` values so the
   template can emit explicit `null` JSON.
2. **Template rendering**: `create_work_package.ftl` produces a complete JSON
   payload with:
   - `subject` (required)
   - `scheduleManually: true` (enables manual date management)
   - `startDate`, `dueDate`, `estimatedTime`, `storyPoints` (conditional —
     null if absent)
   - `duration: null` (explicitly set)
   - `_links.type` → `/api/v3/types/{typeId}`
   - `_links.priority` → conditional, only if `priorityId` is present
   - `_links.project` → `/api/v3/projects/{projectId}`
   - `_links.status` → hardcoded to `/api/v3/statuses/1`
   - `_links.parent` → `{href: null}`
   - `description.raw` (empty string if absent, via `!json_string`)
3. **POST** to `/api/v3/projects/{projectId}/work_packages`
4. **Returns** the `id` from the response JSON.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["workPackageCreate"] --> B["Bean Validation\n(OnCreate + Default)"]
    B --> C["PatchMap.of(ALLOW_NULL_VALUES)"]
    C --> D["render(create_work_package.ftl)"]
    D --> E["JSON payload with _links"]
    E --> F["POST /api/v3/projects/{id}/work_packages"]
    F --> G["return id"]
```

## Update Flow

The `workPackageUpdate` MCP tool accepts a `workPackageId` and a
`WorkPackageUpdateDto`, validates it, and delegates to
`OpenProjectApiClient.workPackageUpdate()`.

1. **Model building**: `PatchMap.of(ALLOW_NULL_VALUES, ...)` includes
   `lockVersion` and all DTO fields.
2. **Template rendering**: `update_work_package.ftl` produces a **partial** JSON
   payload:
   - `lockVersion` (always emitted — required for optimistic locking)
   - `_links.type` and `_links.priority` (conditional, only when present)
   - `subject`, `description.raw`, `startDate`, `dueDate`, `estimatedTime`,
     `storyPoints` (all conditional, only emitted when present)
   - `_meta.validateCustomFields: true` (signals server-side custom field validation)
3. **PATCH** to `/api/v3/work_packages/{workPackageId}`

The lock version is the critical invariant: the client must supply the latest
`lockVersion` from the server. If the server's current version differs, the
update fails with a conflict response.

## Attachment Upload

The `workPackageUploadAttachment` MCP tool accepts `workPackageId`, `fileName`,
`fileContentBase64`, and `fileContentType`:

1. **Base64 decode** — throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the input is not
   valid Base64.
2. **Multipart body** — `restOperations.buildMultipartAttachmentBody()` wraps
   the decoded bytes into a multipart/form-data request.
3. **POST** to `/api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}/attachments`
4. **Returns** the attachment `id`.

## Parent and Child Relations

### Adding a Parent

`RelationTools.relationAddParent(workPackageId, parentWorkPackageId)` performs an
in-band parent relation by patching the target work package:

1. **Fetch** the current work package via `GET /api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}`
   to read the latest `lockVersion`.
2. **Build model** with `PatchMap.of(ALLOW_NULL_VALUES, "lockVersion", ...,
   "parentHref", WP_PREFIX + parentId)`.
3. **Render** `update_parent_relation.ftl`, which emits:
   ```json
   {
     "lockVersion": <current>,
     "_links": {
       "parent": { "href": "/api/v3/work_packages/{parentId}" }
     }
   }
   ```
4. **PATCH** to `/api/v3/work_packages/{workPackageId}`.

### Deleting a Parent

`RelationTools.relationDeleteParent(workPackageId)` follows the same pattern but
sets `parentHref` to `null`, causing the template to emit:

```json
{
  "lockVersion": <current>,
  "_links": {
    "parent": { "href": null }
  }
}
```

### General Relations

`RelationTools.relationAdd()` creates a typed relation between two work packages
via `POST /api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}/relations`, rendering
`create_parent_relation.ftl` to produce a JSON payload with `type`,
`description`, and `_links.to.href`.

`RelationTools.relationDelete()` removes a relation by `DELETE
/api/v3/relations/{relationId}`. On failure (e.g., 404), it logs a warning and
returns `false` rather than throwing.

### Listing Relations

`OpenProjectApiClient.listRelationsForWorkPackage()` assembles the complete
relation set from four sources:

1. **Explicit relations** — from `_embedded.relations._embedded.elements[]` in
   the work package JSON, mapped via `RelationMapper.fromRelationElement()`.
2. **Parent** — derived from `_links.parent`, mapped via
   `RelationMapper.fromWpLink("parent", ...)`.
3. **Children** — derived from `_links.children[]`, mapped via
   `RelationMapper.fromWpLink("children", ...)`.
4. **Ancestors** — derived from `_links.ancestors[]`, mapped via
   `RelationMapper.fromWpLink("ancestors", ...)`.

Derived relations (`parent`, `children`, `ancestors`) have `id = null` because
they are inferred from links, not stored as explicit relation records.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["listRelationsForWorkPackage"] --> B["GET /api/v3/work_packages/{wpId}"]
    B --> C["_embedded.relations\n_explicit relations_"]
    B --> D["_links.parent\n_derived parent_"]
    B --> E["_links.children[]\n_derived children_"]
    B --> F["_links.ancestors[]\n_derived ancestors_"]
    C --> G["Collection<RelationDto>"]
    D --> G
    E --> G
    F --> G
```

## PatchMap Utility

`PatchMap` is a map-creation utility with null-value filtering. It supports two
modes:

- **`ALLOW_NULL_VALUES`**: includes entries where the value is `null` (used for
  work package creation and updates, where explicit `null` must appear in the
  JSON payload).
- **`DROP_NULL_VALUES`**: skips entries with `null` values (used for general
  patch scenarios where absent keys mean "no change").

The constructor validates that the alternating key-value argument count is even.

## Safe Edit Prompt

`WorkPackageTools.safeEditWorkPackagePrompt` provides a structured,
human-in-the-loop workflow for safe work package modifications:

1. **Fetch** the current work package state.
2. **Prepare a diff** showing old vs. new values for all affected fields.
3. **Ask for explicit confirmation** ("Yes, apply", "Confirm", "Proceed").
4. **Execute** `work_package_update` with the latest `lockVersion`.
5. **Reload** after any update before performing further changes.

Key protocol rules enforced by the prompt:

- **Markdown newlines**: represent line breaks as the literal two-character
  sequence `/n` in proposed text (not `\\n`).
- **LockVersion staleness**: after any update, treat the local state as stale
  and always refetch before subsequent changes.
- **Diff before update**: the unified diff must be presented before any
  `work_package_update` call.
- **No silent updates**: updates never apply without explicit user confirmation.

## Validation Failures

| Tool Method | Constraint Violation |
|---|---|
| `workPackageList` | `projectId` is null |
| `workPackageShow` | `workPackageId` is null |
| `workPackageCreate` (no dto) | `projectId` and `workPackage` are null |
| `workPackageCreate` (empty dto) | `subject` is blank, `typeId` is null |
| `workPackageUpdate` (no dto) | `workPackageId` and `workPackage` are null |
| `workPackageUpdate` (empty dto) | `lockVersion` is null |
| `workPackageUploadAttachment` | any of the four params is null |

All validation failures throw `ConstraintViolationException` with property path
identifiers like `workPackageCreate.workPackage.subject` for debugging.

## State Diagram

The work package lifecycle across the MCP tool layer can be summarized as:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> New: workPackageCreate
    New --> Exists: POST succeeds
    Exists --> Updated: workPackageUpdate (lockVersion OK)
    Exists --> Conflict: workPackageUpdate (lockVersion mismatch)
    Updated --> Exists: POST succeeds (re-fetch lockVersion)
    Conflict --> Exists: refetch + retry
    Exists --> Attached: workPackageUploadAttachment
    Attached --> Exists: attachment added
    Exists --> Related: relationAdd / relationAddParent
    Related --> Exists: relation established
    Exists --> Parentless: relationDeleteParent
    Parentless --> Exists: parent removed
```
